questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONSUMES THE HIGHEST ENERGY DURING ASSIMILATION?
questions.explanation:
PROTEINS CONSUME THE HIGHEST ENERGY DURING ASSIMILATION.
THE ENERGY WASTED IN THE ASSIMILATION OF FOOD IS REPRESENTED AS DIET-INDUCED THERMOGENESIS
OR SPECIFIC DYNAMIC ACTION(SDA). DIET-INDUCED THERMOGENESIS (DIT) CAN BE DEFINED AS THE INCREASE
IN ENERGY EXPENDITURE ABOVE THE BASAL METABOLIC RATE AND IS EXPRESSED AS A PERCENTAGE.
THE VALUES FOR DIET-INDUCED THERMOGENESIS ARE RELATIVELY HIGHER PROTEIN AND ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION
AND LOWER AT A HIGH-FAT CONSUMPTION, THE HIERARCHY FOR IT, BEING IN THE SEQUENCE OF ALCOHOL>
PROTEIN> FAT> CARBOHYDRATE. THE VALUE OF DIT FOR PROTEIN IS 30%, THE LIPID IS 15% AND
CARBOHYDRATE IS 5%. HENCE, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE LOSS OF ENERGY AS DIT, ADDITIONAL 10% CALORIES
SHOULD BE PROVIDED IN A MIXED DIET.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE BEST METHOD TO DETECT HBA1C?
questions.explanation:
ION EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY IS THE BEST METHOD TO DETECT HBA1C.
ION-EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY ALLOWS THE SEPARATION OF IONIZABLE MOLECULES ACCORDING TO
DIFFERENCES IN CHARGE. IT INVOLVES THE USE OF A COLUMN WHICH CONTAINS A MATRIX CONSISTING OF
RESIN-BOUND CHARGED GROUPS.
IF THE CHARGED GROUP IS ANIONIC OR NEGATIVELY CHARGED, IT IS CALLED A CATION EXCHANGER AND IS USED IN
CATION EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY WHERE PROTEINS WITH A NET POSITIVE CHARGE MIGRATE THROUGH THE
MATRIX MORE SLOWLY THAN THOSE WITH A NET NEGATIVE CHARGE DUE TO RETARDATION OF THE MIGRATION OF
THE FORMER WHICH IS ATTRACTED TO THE NEGATIVE CHARGES BOUND TO THE RESIN. CATION EXCHANGE
CHROMATOGRAPHY IS USED FOR NEGATIVELY CHARGED HBA1C ESTIMATION AND IS USED AS A DIAGNOSTIC TOOL
FOR DIABETES MELLITUS.
GLYCATED HEMOGLOBIN, REPORTED AS HBA1C, HAS BEEN USED TO MONITOR GLYCEMIC CONTROL IN PATIENTS
WITH DIABETES FOR MANY YEARS. HBA1C RESULTS FROM THE ATTACHMENT OF GLUCOSE TO THE N-TERMINAL
809
VALINE OF THE HEMOGLOBIN β-CHAIN.
THE CONCENTRATION OF HBA1C DEPENDS ON BOTH THE CONCENTRATION OF GLUCOSE IN THE BLOOD AND THE
LIFESPAN OF THE ERYTHROCYTE. SINCE THE HALF-LIFE OF AN RBC IS 60 DAYS, THE LEVEL OF GLYCATED
HAEMOGLOBIN REFLECTS THE MEAN BLOOD GLUCOSE CONCENTRATION OVER THE PRECEDING 6 TO 8 WEEKS.
NORMAL GLUCOSE TOLERANCE IS CHARACTERIZED BY AN HBA1C < 5.7%; ANY VALUE OF HBA1C EQUAL TO OR
EXCEEDING 6.5 % IS DIAGNOSTIC OF THE PATIENT BEING DIABETIC. ALSO, ION EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY
HAS THE ADVANTAGE OF SEPARATING HEMOGLOBIN VARIANTS INTO PEAKS WITH THE LEAST INTERFERENCE BY
OTHER HEMOGLOBIN VARIANTS; ITS DISADVANTAGE IS THAT IT IS TEMPERATURE DEPENDANT.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: ELECTROPHORESIS IS AN ELECTROCHEMICAL PROCESS WHERE MACROMOLECULES OR COLLOIDAL
PARTICLES DEPENDING ON THE ELECTRIC CHARGE MIGRATE IN A SOLUTION UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF AN ELECTRIC
CURRENT. IT CAN ALSO BE USED FOR HBA1C ESTIMATION, ITS ADVANTAGE BEING ABLE TO IDENTIFY DIFFERENT
VARIANTS OF HAEMOGLOBIN AND DISADVANTAGE BEING INTERFERENCE OF THE PROCESS BY FETAL
HEMOGLOBIN(HBF).
OPTION C: IMMUNOASSAYS ARE USED TO QUANTIFY MOLECULES BASED ON THE SPECIFICITY AND SELECTIVITY OF
ANTIBODY REAGENTS GENERATED. IT CAN PROVIDE QUANTITATIVE ESTIMATES OF HBA1C BUT HBF PRODUCES
FALSELY LOW RESULTS AND HEMOGLOBIN VARIANTS SUCH AS HBS AND HBC MAY CAUSE A FALSE INCREASE
IN HBA1C MEASUREMENTS.
OPTION D: AFFINITY CHROMATOGRAPHY IS A TYPE OF LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY. IT INVOLVES THE PASSING OF A
MATRIX THROUGH A SOLUTION THAT CONSISTS OF THE MOLECULES OF INTEREST. THESE MOLECULES WOULD HAVE A
SPECIFIC AFFINITY FOR LIGANDS PRESENT IN THE MATRIX AND BIND WITH THEM AND END UP GETTING SEPARATED
FROM THE SOLUTION. IT CAN BE USED TO MEASURE HBA1C WITHOUT BEING AFFECTED BY TEMPERATURE. HIGH
LEVELS OF HBF SEEN IN THALASSEMIA MAY INTERFERE WITH ITS RESULT.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING OPTIONS IS FALSE IN A PATIENT WITH ADVANCED LIVER DISEASE?
options: INCREASED SYNTHESIS OF GLUTAMINE AND GLUTAMATE FROM ALPHA-KETOGLUTARATE
questions.explanation:
OXIDATIVE DECARBOXYLATION OF ALPHA-KETOGLUTARATE IS NOT SEEN IN A PATIENT WITH ADVANCED LIVER
DISEASE. OPTION C IS FALSE.
NORMALLY, AMMONIA, A TOXIC BY-PRODUCT OF PROTEIN CATABOLISM, IS EXCRETED AS UREA UPON BEING
METABOLISED IN THE UREA CYCLE, WHICH TAKES PLACE IN THE LIVER. IN ADVANCED LIVER DISEASE, IMPAIRED
AMMONIA METABOLISM LEADS TO HYPERAMMONEMIA. AMMONIA WITHDRAWS α-KETOGLUTARATE TO FORM
GLUTAMATE AND GLUTAMINE. THIS LEADS TO LOWERED CONCENTRATIONS OF ALL CITRIC ACID CYCLE
INTERMEDIATES, AND HENCE REDUCED GENERATION OF ATP.
THE KREBS CYCLE INVOLVES A SEQUENCE OF REACTIONS OCCURRING IN MITOCHONDRIA THAT OXIDIZE THE ACETYL
MOIETY OF ACETYL-COA TO CO2 AND REDUCES THE COENZYMES THAT ARE REOXIDIZED THROUGH THE ELECTRON
TRANSPORT CHAIN. IT IS THE FINAL COMMON PATHWAY FOR THE OXIDATION OF CARBOHYDRATES, LIPIDS, AND
PROTEIN ALSO HAS A CENTRAL ROLE IN GLUCONEOGENESIS, LIPOGENESIS, AND INTERCONVERSION OF AMINO ACIDS.
ALTHOUGH PROCESSES OCCUR IN MANY TISSUES, THE LIVER IS THE ONLY TISSUE IN WHICH ALL OCCUR TO A
SIGNIFICANT EXTENT.
THE REACTIONS THAT OCCUR IN KREB'S CYCLE ARE SHOWN IN THE IMAGE BELOW.
810
ONE OF THE STEPS OF THE KREBS CYCLE INVOLVES α-KETOGLUTARATE UNDERGOING OXIDATIVE DECARBOXYLATION
IN A REACTION CATALYZED BY α-KETOGLUTARATE DEHYDROGENASE, RESULTING IN THE FORMATION OF
SUCCINYL-COA. HIGH CONCENTRATIONS OF AMMONIA INHIBIT α-KETOGLUTARATE DEHYDROGENASE, THEREBY
PREVENTING ITS OXIDATIVE DECARBOXYLATION.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS ASSOCIATED WITH A DEFECT IN COLLAGEN MATURITY?
questions.explanation:
SCURVY IS ASSOCIATED WITH A DEFECT IN COLLAGEN MATURITY.
SCURVY RESULTS FROM ASCORBIC ACID OR VITAMIN C DEFICIENCY. VITAMIN C IS AN ESSENTIAL COFACTOR FOR
THE ENZYME PROLYL HYDROXYLASE, REQUIRED FOR THE HYDROXYLATION OF PROLYL RESIDUES IN COLLAGEN. THIS
ENABLES EACH COLLAGEN FIBRIL TO FORM A UNIFORM AND FLEXIBLE TRIPLE HELIX CONFIGURATION IN THE BODY’S
CONNECTIVE TISSUES.
ITS DEFICIENCY RESULTS IN A DEFECTIVE PROLYL HYDROXYLASE ACTIVITY, THEREBY RESULTING IN THE IMPAIRED
FORMATION OF MATURE CONNECTIVE TISSUE; THE CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF THIS DEFICIENCY
INCLUDE PETECHIAE, ECCHYMOSIS, COILED HAIRS, INFLAMED AND BLEEDING GUMS, JOINT EFFUSION, TOOTH
LOSS, BONE FRACTURE, POOR WOUND HEALING, AND FATIGUE WHICH CAN BE ATTRIBUTED TO IMPAIRED COLLAGEN
SYNTHESIS ALL OF WHICH ARE TYPICAL OF SCURVY.
RISK FACTORS INCLUDE CHRONIC ALCOHOLISM, DISEASES SUCH AS CELIAC DISEASE AND CROHN’S DISEASE,
ASSOCIATED WITH MALABSORPTION AND POOR NUTRITION.
IT IS TREATED WITH VITAMIN C SUPPLEMENTATION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B- RICKETS IS CAUSED DUE TO DEFICIENCY OF VITAMIN D IN CHILDREN WHICH IS CHARACTERIZED BY
THE CONTINUED FORMATION OF THE COLLAGEN MATRIX OF BONE BUT ITS INCOMPLETE MINERALIZATION OR
DEMINERALIZATION. CHILDREN HAVE SOFT, PLIABLE BONES.
OPTION C- BERIBERI IS CAUSED DUE TO DEFICIENCY OF THIAMINE. IT CAN EITHER BE DRY BERIBERI
CHARACTERIZED BY PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY OR WET BERIBERI CHARACTERIZED BY EDEMA DUE TO DILATED
CARDIOMYOPATHY.
811
OPTION D- NIGHT BLINDNESS IS CAUSED BY A DEFICIENCY OF VITAMIN A. DEFICIENCY CAN ALSO LEAD TO
PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY, REPEATED GASTROINTESTINAL, PULMONARY, AND URINARY INFECTIONS, AND
XEROPTHALMIA.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT A SUBSTRATE FOR GLUCOSE FORMATION?
questions.explanation:
ACETYL COENZYME A (COA) IS NOT A SUBSTRATE FOR GLUCOSE FORMATION.
ACETYL COA AND COMPOUNDS THAT GIVE RISE TO ACETYL COA ALONE LIKE ACETOACETATE, LYSINE, AND LEUCINE
CANNOT GIVE RISE TO A NET SYNTHESIS OF GLUCOSE. THIS IS BECAUSE OF THE IRREVERSIBLE NATURE OF THE
PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX, WHICH CONVERTS PYRUVATE TO ACETYL COA. THESE COMPOUNDS GIVE
RISE TO KETONE BODIES INSTEAD.
THE SYNTHESIS OF GLUCOSE IN THE BODY, IN THE ABSENCE OF DIETARY CARBOHYDRATES, OCCURS IN TWO WAYS:
- FROM LIVER GLYCOGEN, BY A PROCESS KNOWN AS GLYCOGENOLYSIS IN THE ABSENCE OF DIETARY
CARBOHYDRATE, FOR UP TO 24 HOURS.
- DE NOVO, FROM NON-CARBOHYDRATE SOURCES, BY A PROCESS KNOWN AS GLUCONEOGENESIS, WHEN
GLYCOGEN STORES HAVE DEPLETED. THIS OCCURS PRIMARILY IN THE LIVER AND TO A LESSER EXTENT IN THE
KIDNEYS WHILE FASTING OVERNIGHT OR PRIMARILY IN THE KIDNEYS DURING PROLONGED FASTING OF 48 HOURS
OR LONGER.
THE SUBSTRATE FOR GLYCOGENOLYSIS IS GLYCOGEN AND DURING THIS PROCESS, GLYCOGEN IS FIRST CONVERTED
INTO GLUCOSE-1-PHOSPHATE BY THE ENZYME GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE. THIS IS A RATE-LIMITING STEP IN THE
PROCESS. GLUCOSE-1-PHOSPHATE IS THEN CONVERTED TO GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE BY THE ENZYME
PHOSPHOGLUCOMUTASE AND EVENTUALLY, GLUCOSE IS OBTAINED FROM GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE BY THE ENZYME
PHOSPHATASE. THERE IS NO INVOLVEMENT OF ACETYL COA.
THE STEPS WITH ENZYMES INVOLVED IN GLYCOGENOLYSIS ARE SHOWN IN THE IMAGE BELOW.
IN GLUCONEOGENESIS, THE SUBSTRATES CAN BE:
812
- OXALOACETATE (FROM ITS CONJUGATE ACID, OXALOACETIC ACID) IS A DIRECT PRECURSOR OF
PHOSPHOENOLPYRUVATE
- PYRUVATE, AN α-KETO ACID THAT CAN BE CONVERTED TO GLUCOSE. ALANINE IS A GLUCOGENIC AMINO ACID
THAT IS TRANSAMINATED TO FORM PYRUVATE BY THE ENZYME ALANINE AMINO-TRANSFERASE IN THE LIVER; THE
PYRUVATE FORMED, CAN BE USED FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF GLUCOSE.
- LACTATE, OBTAINED FROM ANAEROBIC GLYCOLYSIS, RELEASED FROM SKELETAL MUSCLES AND RBCS INTO THE
BLOOD, TO BE TAKEN UP BY THE LIVER IN THE CORI CYCLE TO BE OXIDISED TO PYRUVATE, TO EVENTUALLY
SYNTHESIZE GLUCOSE
- GLYCEROL FROM ADIPOSE TISSUE IS CONVERTED TO DIHYDROXYACETONE PHOSPHATE IN THE LIVER, WHICH
ITSELF IS AN INTERMEDIATE OF GLYCOLYSIS AND GLUCONEOGENESIS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE BEST TEST FOR QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF AN RNA SAMPLE?
options: RTPCR FOLLOWED BY REAL TIME PCR
questions.answer: RTPCR FOLLOWED BY REAL TIME PCR
questions.explanation:
RTPCR FOLLOWED BY REAL-TIME PCR IS THE BEST TEST FOR QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF AN RNA SAMPLE.
RTPCR (REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE PCR) INVOLVES THE GENERATION OF COMPLEMENTARY DNA (CDNA) COPIES
OF THE MRNA USING THE REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE ENZYME FOLLOWED BY AMPLIFICATION OF THE CDNA COPIES
BY PCR TECHNIQUE.
QUANTIFICATION OF DNA INVOLVES THE ASSESSMENT OF THE AMOUNT/CONCENTRATION OF DNA THAT IS
PRESENT IN A SAMPLE WHEN CARRYING OUT A TECHNIQUE LIKE PCR. REAL-TIME PCR OR QUANTITATIVE
PCR/QPCR INVOLVES THE QUANTIFICATION OF DNA AFTER EACH CYCLE OF AMPLIFICATION, OR, IN "REAL-TIME"
THAN AT THE END OF THE PROCEDURE; THEREFORE REAL-TIME PCR HELPS IN QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF DNA.
WHEN REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE PCR AND QPCR ARE COMBINED, THEY CAN BE USED TO DETERMINE THE
RELATIVE CONCENTRATIONS OF A PARTICULAR MRNA MOLECULE IN A CELL.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: REAL-TIME PCR ALONE CAN ONLY BE USED FOR THE QUANTIFICATION OF DNA ONLY.
813
OPTION B: RTPCR CAN CONVERT THE RNA INTO CDNA BY REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE ENZYME AND THEN
AMPLIFY THE CDNA COPIES BY MEANS OF PCR BUT CANNOT QUANTIFY THE DNA/RNA.
OPTION C: PCR-RESTRICTION FRAGMENT LENGTH POLYMORPHISM (PCR-RFLP) IS ALSO CALLED CLEAVED
AMPLIFIED POLYMORPHIC SEQUENCE (CAPS) ASSAY. POLYMORPHISMS ARE INHERITED DIFFERENCES FOUND
AMONG INDIVIDUALS IN MORE THAN 1% OF THE NORMAL POPULATION. PCR-RFLP IS A TECHNIQUE IN WHICH
ORGANISMS MAY BE DIFFERENTIATED BY VARIATIONS IN THEIR DNA SEQUENCE BY RESTRICTION
ENDONUCLEASES. TYPICALLY, GEL ELECTROPHORESIS IS USED TO VISUALIZE RFLPS. THUS, DNA BUT NOT RNA
MOLECULES CAN BE QUANTIFIED IN THIS PROCESS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WOBBLE HYPOTHESIS EXPLAINS WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONCEPTS OF THE GENETIC CODE?
questions.explanation:
THE WOBBLE HYPOTHESIS EXPLAINS THE DEGENERACY OF THE GENETIC CODE.
THE WOBBLE HYPOTHESIS STATES THAT CODON-ANTICODON PAIRING FOLLOWS THE TRADITIONAL WATSON–CRICK
RULES (G PAIRS WITH C AND A PAIRS WITH U) FOR THE FIRST TWO BASES OF THE CODON BUT CAN BE LESS
STRINGENT FOR THE THIRD/LAST BASE. IT HAS BEEN OBSERVED THAT A TRNA CAN RECOGNIZE MORE THAN ONE
CODON FOR A SPECIFIC AMINO ACID, ESPECIALLY IN THE LAST NUCLEOTIDE OF THE CODON TRIPLET. THIS IS
REFERRED TO AS DEGENERACY AND ITS MECHANISM CAN BE EXPLAINED BY THE WOBBLE HYPOTHESIS.
THE FIRST BASE OF THE ANTICODON MOVES TO PERMIT NONTRADITIONAL PAIRING WITH THE LAST BASE OF THE
CODON. THIS MOVEMENT IS CALLED WOBBLE AND IS POSSIBLE BECAUSE THE FIRST BASE OF THE ANTICODON IS
NOT AS SPATIALLY DEFINED AS THE OTHER TWO BASES. DUE TO THE WOBBLING, 61 TRNA SPECIES ARE NOT
REQUIRED TO READ THE 61 CODONS.
FOR EXAMPLE, THREE CODONS FOR GLYCINE—GGU, GGC, AND GGA—CAN FORM A BASE PAIR FROM ONE
ANTICODON, 3′ CCI 5′ IE, I, INOSINE, CAN BASE PAIR WITH U, C, AND A, AS SHOWN IN THE DIAGRAM BELOW.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE GENETIC CODE IS UNIVERSAL BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME FOR ALL LIVING ORGANISMS.
OPTION B: THE GENETIC CODE IS UNAMBIGUOUS BECAUSE EACH CODON IS SPECIFIC FOR ONLY ONE AMINO
ACID. EXAMPLE: GGA ONLY CODES FOR GLYCINE.
OPTION D: THE GENETIC CODE IS NON-PUNCTUATED. THIS MEANS THAT ONCE THE READING COMMENCES AT A
SPECIFIC START CODON, IT IS CONTINUOUS AND IS READ CONTINUOUSLY AS TRIPLETS UNTIL A STOP CODON IS
REACHED WITHOUT STOPPING.
814

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS ARE TRUE REGARDING MITOCHONDRIAL DNA?
questions.explanation:
STATEMENTS 1 AND 2 ARE TRUE REGARDING MITOCHONDRIAL DNA; IT HAS A HIGHER RATE OF MUTATIONS AS
COMPARED TO THE NUCLEAR GENOME AND IS A CIRCULAR DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA WITH ABOUT 16,000 BASE
PAIRS.
MITOCHONDRIAL DNA IS CIRCULAR, DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA COMPOSED OF HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAINS AND
COMPRISES ABOUT 1% OF TOTAL CELLULAR DNA. IT CONTAINS ABOUT 16,569 BASE PAIRS AND ENCODES ABOUT
13 PROTEIN SUBUNITS OF THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN, OF A TOTAL OF ABOUT 67 PROTEIN SUBUNITS.
ITS GENETIC CODE/ NUCLEOTIDE SEQUENCE LARGELY DIFFERS FROM THAT OF THE STANDARD CELLULAR CODE. FOR
EXAMPLE, THE STANDARD STOP CODON UGA IS READ AS TRYPTOPHAN (TRP); IN ADDITION, FEW UNTRANSLATED
SEQUENCES EXIST AND A VERY HIGH MUTATION RATE, ABOUT 5-10 TIMES COMPARED TO THAT OF NUCLEAR DNA
OF THE CELL IS OBSERVED.
AS ALL MITOCHONDRIA ARE CONTRIBUTED BY THE OVUM DURING ZYGOTE FORMATION, HUMAN MITOCHONDRIAL
DNA IS TRANSMITTED BY MATERNAL NON-MENDELIAN INHERITANCE. THIS IS CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE
IN DISEASES RESULTING FROM MUTATIONS OF MITOCHONDRIAL DNA, EXCEPT IN A FEW CASES, AN AFFECTED
MOTHER WOULD PASS THE DISEASE TO ALL OF HER CHILDREN BUT ONLY HER DAUGHTERS WOULD TRANSMIT THE
TRAIT.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE REPAIR MECHANISM ASSOCIATED WITH CRISPR-CAS9?
questions.explanation:
THE REPAIR MECHANISM ASSOCIATED WITH CRISPR-CAS9 IS NON-HOMOLOGOUS END-JOINING.
NON-HOMOLOGOUS END-JOINING (NHEJ) IS A MECHANISM BY WHICH A GROUP OF PROTEINS MEDIATES THE
RECOGNITION, PROCESSING, AND DIRECT LIGATION OF THE ENDS OF TWO DNA FRAGMENTS WHERE A
DOUBLE-STRAND BREAK IN DNA HAS OCCURRED. THIS IS IN CONTRAST TO HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION (HR),
ANOTHER MECHANISM TO REPAIR A DOUBLE-STRAND BREAK, WHERE DNA REPAIR NEEDS AN UNDAMAGED
HOMOLOGOUS DNA TEMPLATE TO REPLACE AN ADJACENT DAMAGED ONE.
CLUSTERED REGULARLY INTERSPACED SHORT PALINDROMIC REPEATS-ASSOCIATED GENE 9 OR CRISPR-CAS9 IS
A DNA EDITING/GENE REGULATORY SYSTEM. IT INVOLVES TWO ESSENTIAL COMPONENTS, CAS9, AN
ENDONUCLEASE THAT CAUSES A DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA BREAK, ALLOWING MODIFICATIONS TO THE GENOMIC
DNA TO BE MADE; AND A SYNTHETIC SINGLE GUIDE RNA OR SGRNA RESPONSIBLE FOR GUIDING CAS9 TO ITS
TARGET.
ONCE THE SGRNA HAS DIRECTED THE CAS9 TO THE SECTION OF THE GENOMIC DNA TO BE EDITED, THE 3’ END
OF THE SGRNA COMES TO LIE ACROSS A SPECIFIC SEQUENCE OF DNA ADJACENT TO THE EDITING SIDE CALLED THE
PROTOSPACER ADJACENT MOTIF OR PAM. THE CAS9 NOW CAUSES A DOUBLE-STRANDED BREAK IN THE DNA AT
THE PAM SITE WHICH IS THEN REPAIRED BY A NON-HOMOLOGOUS END-JOINING.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH THIAMINE DEFICIENCY DEVELOPS LACTIC ACIDOSIS. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING ENZYMES IS
AFFECTED?
questions.explanation:
PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE IS THE ENZYME AFFECTED IN A PATIENT WITH THIAMINE DEFICIENCY WHO DEVELOPS
LACTIC ACIDOSIS.
PYRUVATE IS TRANSPORTED FROM THE CYTOSOL INTO THE MITOCHONDRIA, WHERE UNDERGOES OXIDATIVE
DECARBOXYLATION TO FORM ACETYL COA IN THE PRESENCE OF THE MULTI-ENZYME PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE
COMPLEX (PDHC) IN THE MITOCHONDRIAL MATRIX.
THE PDHC PRIMARILY CONSISTS OF THREE ENZYMES: PYRUVATE DECARBOXYLASE (ALSO CALLED PYRUVATE
DEHYDROGENASE), DIHYDROLIPOYL TRANSACETYLASE, AND DIHYDROLIPOYL DEHYDROGENASE. IT ALSO REQUIRES
THE FOLLOWING CO-ENZYMES:
- THIAMINE PYROPHOSPHATE, ESSENTIAL FOR PYRUVATE DECARBOXYLASE AND IS TIGHTLY BOUND TO IT
- LIPOIC ACID AND COENZYME A, ESSENTIAL FOR DIHYDROLIPOYL TRANSACETYLASE
- FAD AND NAD+, ESSENTIAL FOR DIHYDROLIPOYL DEHYDROGENASE.
IN A PATIENT WITH THIAMINE DEFICIENCY, DUE TO THE INACTIVE THIAMINE PYROPHOSPHATE, THE PYRUVATE
DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX IS UNABLE TO ACT ON PYRUVATE, WHICH BEGINS TO ACCUMULATE ON THE BODY AND
IS THEN SHUNTED TOWARDS LACTIC ACID FORMATION BY THE ENZYME LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE.
THIS RESULTS IN LACTIC ACID ACCUMULATION AND SUBSEQUENT LACTIC ACIDOSIS IN THE PATIENT.
WERNICKE–KORSAKOFF, AN ENCEPHALOPATHY-PSYCHOSIS SYNDROME DUE TO THIAMINE DEFICIENCY, MAY BE
SEEN IN CHRONIC ALCOHOLICS. IT OCCURS DUE TO INSUFFICIENT PRODUCTION OF ATP BY THE BRAIN CELLS VIA THE
CITRIC ACID CYCLE AS THE PDHC IS INACTIVE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: PYRUVATE CARBOXYLASE FACILITATES THE CONVERSION OF PYRUVATE TO OXALOACETATE BY
CARBOXYLATION.
OPTION C: PHOSPHOENOLPYRUVATE CARBOXYKINASE IS INVOLVED IN THE DECARBOXYLATION AND
PHOSPHORYLATION OF OXALOACETATE TO FORM PHOSPHOENOLPYRUVATE SEEN IN GLUCONEOGENESIS.
817
OPTION D: TRANSKETOLASE WITH COENZYME THIAMINE PYROPHOSPHATE IS AN ENZYME INVOLVED IN THE
NON-OXIDATIVE PHASE OF THE PENTOSE PHOSPHATE PATHWAY.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT AMPHIPATHIC?
questions.explanation:
TRIGLYCERIDES ARE NOT AMPHIPATHIC.
AMPHIPATHIC SUBSTANCES ARE THOSE WHICH HAVE BOTH A HYDROPHILIC OR POLAR REGION AND A
HYDROPHOBIC OR NONPOLAR REGION.
PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS OR GLYCEROL-BASED PHOSPHOLIPIDS HAVE A HYDROPHILIC HEAD WHICH IS A PHOSPHATE
GROUP WITH ALCOHOL ATTACHED TO IT AND A HYDROPHOBIC TAIL CONTAINING FATTY ACIDS OR FATTY ACID-BASED
HYDROCARBONS. THEREFORE, THEY ARE AMPHIPATHIC.
SPHINGOLIPIDS, LIKE ALL MEMBRANE-BASED LIPIDS, ARE AMPHIPATHIC MOLECULES HAVING HYDROPHOBIC
AND HYDROPHILIC PROPERTIES.
GLYCOLIPIDS ARE AMPHIPATHIC MOLECULES CONSISTING OF A HYDROPHILIC OLIGOSACCHARIDE CHAIN ATTACHED
TO A HYDROPHOBIC LIPID THAT ANCHORS THE GLYCOLIPID IN CELL MEMBRANES.
BUT LIPIDS LIKE TRIACYLGLYCEROL AND CHOLESTERYL ESTERS ARE TERMED NEUTRAL LIPIDS AND THUS ARE NOT
AMPHIPATHIC.
CHOLESTEROL IS AMPHIPATHIC.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING TESTS WILL BE POSITIVE IN THE URINE OF A PATIENT WHO HAS UNDERGONE
PROLONGED STARVATION?
questions.explanation:
ONLY TEST 3, WHICH IS ROTHERA'S TEST FOR KETONE BODIES IN THE URINE WILL BE POSITIVE IN THE URINE OF A
PATIENT WITH PROLONGED STARVING.
URINE TESTS
TEST 1 - BENEDICT’S TEST FOR REDUCING SUGARS
818
TEST 2 - HEAT AND ACETIC ACID TEST FOR PRESENCE OF ALBUMIN
TEST 3 - ROTHERA’S TEST FOR KETONE BODIES
IN CASE OF PROLONGED STARVATION,
- AFTER A MEAL TILL ABOUT 2 HOURS LATER, MAINTENANCE OF BLOOD GLUCOSE IS PRIMARILY FROM THE DIET.
DURING THIS TIME, HEPATIC GLYCOGEN STORES ARE GETTING REPLENISHED.
- AS DIETARY BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS START TO DECLINE, GLUCAGON SECRETION INCREASES AND INSULIN
SECRETION DECREASES, RESULTING IN RAPID MOBILISATION OF HEPATIC GLYCOGEN STORES.
- IF THERE IS FASTING FOR A LONGER PERIOD OF TIME, HEPATIC GLYCOGEN STORES CANNOT MAINTAIN BLOOD
GLUCOSE LEVELS. 12 HOURS AFTER THE LAST MEAL, GLUCONEOGENESIS BECOMES THE PRIMARY SOURCE OF BLOOD
GLUCOSE, SINCE MOST OF THE HEPATIC GLYCOGEN WOULD HAVE DEPLETED. IF AN INDIVIDUAL CONTINUES
FASTING, GLUCONEOGENESIS CONTINUES TO BE THE MAIN SOURCE.
- HOWEVER, OVER THE FIRST FEW DAYS OF FASTING, KETOGENESIS HAPPENS. THIS IS WHEN THE CONCENTRATION
OF ACETYL COA FROM FATTY ACID OXIDATION EXCEEDS THE OXIDATIVE CAPACITY OF THE TCA CYCLE. ALSO,
KETOGENESIS RELEASES COA, ENSURING ITS AVAILABILITY FOR CONTINUED FATTY ACID OXIDATION.
WATER-SOLUBLE KETONE BODIES ARE USED AS FUEL BY MOST TISSUES, INCLUDING THE BRAIN DURING FASTING. IT
ALSO REDUCES THE NEED FOR GLUCONEOGENESIS FROM AMINO ACID CARBON SKELETONS, THUS PRESERVING
ESSENTIAL PROTEIN IN THE BODY.
THEREFORE, DURING PROLONGED FASTING, THE LEVELS OF KETONE BODIES IN THE BODY RISE AND SUBSEQUENTLY
BEGIN TO BE ELIMINATED IN URINE. HENCE, IN STARVATION KETOSIS, ROTHERA'S TEST WILL BE POSITIVE, BUT
BENEDICT'S TEST WILL BE NEGATIVE.
BOTH BENEDICT'S AND ROTHERA'S TESTS WILL BE POSITIVE IN DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS. (OPTION 1)
- BENEDICT'S TEST (TEST 1) FOR REDUCING SUGARS IS A SEMIQUANTITATIVE METHOD FOR THE ESTIMATION OF
SUGAR IN THE URINE.
- ROTHERA'S TEST (TEST 3) IS PERFORMED BY SATURATING URINE WITH SOLID AMMONIUM SULFATE. ON ADDING
SODIUM NITROPRUSSIDE AND LIQUOR AMMONIA ALONG THE SIDES OF THE TEST TUBE, A PURPLE RING IS FORMED
AT THE JUNCTION OF THE TWO LIQUIDS IF THERE IS ACETONE OR ACETOACETIC ACID IN URINE.
BETA-HYDROXYBUTYRATE DOES NOT GIVE A PURPLE RING.
- HEAT AND ACETIC ACID TEST (TEST 2) FOR PROTEINURIA IS BASED ON THE FACT THAT WHEN HEATED TO AN
ISOELECTRIC POINT, PROTEINS GET COAGULATED.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
THE ACTION OF INHIBITION OF ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE ENZYME BY ORGANOPHOSPHORUS COMPOUNDS IS
THROUGH WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING MECHANISMS?
options:
SUICIDAL INHIBITION
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
THE ACTION OF INHIBITION ON ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE ENZYME BY ORGANOPHOSPHORUS COMPOUNDS IS
THROUGH IRREVERSIBLE COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.
COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS A TYPE OF INHIBITION THAT OCCURS WHEN THE INHIBITOR BINDS REVERSIBLY TO THE
SAME SITE THAT THE SUBSTRATE WOULD NORMALLY OCCUPY. IT, THEREFORE, COMPETES WITH THE SUBSTRATE FOR
BINDING TO THE ENZYME ACTIVE SITE. THE EFFECT OF COMPETITIVE INHIBITION CAN BE OVERCOME BY
INCREASING THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE. KM IS INCREASED, BUT VMAX IS UNALTERED IN THIS TYPE
OF INHIBITION.
COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS OF TWO TYPES:
- IRREVERSIBLE (NON-EQUILIBRIUM TYPE) COMPETITIVE INHIBITION: THE INHIBITOR FORMS STRONG COVALENT
BONDS OR HAS SUCH A HIGH AFFINITY FOR THE ENZYME THAT THE NORMAL SUBSTRATE IS NOT ABLE TO DISPLACE
THE INHIBITOR. FOR EXAMPLE, ORGANOPHOSPHORUS POISONING INHIBITS ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE(ACHE).
ONCE AN ORGANOPHOSPHATE BINDS TO ACHE, ENDOGENOUS HYDROLYSIS OF THE PHOSPHORYLATED ENZYME
BY ESTERASES FURTHER LEADS TO IRREVERSIBLE BINDING AND PERMANENT ENZYME INACTIVATION WHICH IS
TERMED AGING.
- REVERSIBLE (EQUILIBRIUM TYPE) COMPETITIVE INHIBITION: SUBSTRATE CONCENTRATION IS SUFFICIENTLY
INCREASED, IT CAN DISPLACE THE INHIBITOR. STATIN DRUG INHIBITS HMG COA REDUCTASE.
NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS BIND TO ENZYMES AT REMOTE SITES FROM THE ACTIVE SITE. THEREFORE,
NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITION CANNOT BE OVERCOME BY INCREASING THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE.
THUS, NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS DECREASE THE VMAX OF THE REACTION. THEY DO NOT INTERFERE WITH THE
BINDING OF THE SUBSTRATE TO THE ENZYME. THUS, THE ENZYME SHOWS THE SAME KM IN THE PRESENCE OR
ABSENCE OF NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS. FOR EG, ACETAZOLAMIDE INHIBITS CARBONIC ANHYDRASE, DIGOXIN
INHIBITS NA+ K+ ATPASE
GRAPH SHOWING THE CHANGES IN VMAX AND KM NONCOMPETITIVE AND COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.
820
SUICIDAL INHIBITION IS A SPECIAL TYPE OF IRREVERSIBLE INHIBITION. IT IS ALSO KNOWN AS MECHANISM-BASED
INACTIVATION. THE INHIBITOR IS A SPECIALISED SUBSTRATE ANALOG THAT CAN BE TRANSFORMED BY THE ENZYME
IT IS INHIBITING. AFTER BINDING TO THE ACTIVE SITE OF THE ENZYME, A HIGHLY REACTIVE GROUP IS GENERATED.
THIS COVALENTLY BINDS TO AND INHIBITS THE ENZYME. AN EXAMPLE IS ALLOPURINOL, WHICH IS OXIDISED BY
XANTHINE OXIDASE TO ALLOXANTHINE. ALLOXANTHINE IN TURN IS A STRONG INHIBITOR OF XANTHINE OXIDASE.
821

questions.prompt:
AN ALCOHOLIC PATIENT PRESENTED WITH ITCHY LESIONS AS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE, HE ALSO HAS A
RED-COLORED BEEFY TONGUE. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING HISTORIES WOULD YOU LIKE TO ADDITIONALLY ASK/
ELICIT IN THIS PATIENT?
options: ASK FOR DIARRHEA AND HISTORY OF MEMORY LOSS
ASK FOR DIARRHEA, THIAMINE DEFICIENCY FEATURES, AND DETAILED DIETARY HISTORY
questions.answer: ASK FOR DIARRHEA AND HISTORY OF MEMORY LOSS
questions.explanation:
AN ALCOHOLIC PATIENT WITH A RED-COLORED BEEFY TONGUE, ITCHING AND THE CHARACTERISTIC CASAL'S
NECKLACE, SHOWN IN THE IMAGE, IS SUGGESTIVE OF PELLAGRA. IT IS CAUSED BY NIACIN/VITAMIN B3
DEFICIENCY. HENCE, ONE SHOULD ASK FOR A HISTORY OF DIARRHEA AND MEMORY LOSS IN THIS CASE.
PELLAGRA PRESENTS WITH 4 DS: DIARRHEA, DERMATITIS, DEMENTIA, AND IF UNTREATED, DEATH. EARLY
SYMPTOMS OF PELLAGRA ARE LOSS OF APPETITE, GENERALIZED WEAKNESS AND IRRITABILITY, ABDOMINAL PAIN,
AND VOMITING. PHOTOSENSITIVE DERMATITIS IS SEEN OVER SUN-EXPOSED AREAS. DIARRHEA OCCURS DUE TO
PROCTITIS OR MALABSORPTION. BRIGHT RED GLOSSITIS (BEEFY TONGUE) AND CASAL’S NECKLACE (A PIGMENTED,
SCALY SKIN RASH THAT FORMS A RING AROUND THE NECK) FOLLOW. DEPRESSIVE PSYCHOSIS AND DEMENTIA ALSO
COMMONLY OCCUR.
CORN/ MAIZE/ JOWAR BASED DIETS ARE THE MAIN CAUSES OF NIACIN DEFICIENCY. CORN/MAIZE LACKS NIACIN
AND TRYPTOPHAN. THE EXCESS LEUCINE IN JOWAR AND MAIZE DISRUPTS THE CONVERSION OF TRYPTOPHAN TO
NIACIN. NIACIN DEFICIENCY IS ALSO SEEN IN ALCOHOLISM. HENCE, ADDITIONAL HISTORIES OF DIARRHEA AND
MEMORY LOSS WILL AID IN SUPPORTING THE DIAGNOSIS OF PELLAGRA (ALONG WITH DIETARY HISTORY).
TREATMENT INCLUDES ORAL SUPPLEMENTATION WITH 100–200 MG OF NICOTINAMIDE OR NICOTINIC ACID
THREE TIMES DAILY FOR 5 DAYS.
OPTION B: THIAMINE DEFICIENCY (VITAMIN B1) FEATURES INCLUDE CVS MANIFESTATIONS LIKE HEART FAILURE
AND EDEMA (WET BERIBERI), PERIPHERAL NEURITIS (DRY BERIBERI), AND WERNICKE ENCEPHALOPATHY (IN
ALCOHOLICS).
OPTION C: DERMATITIS SEEN IN PELLAGRA IS DUE TO DIETARY DEFICIENCY OF NIACIN AND SO ALLERGY HISTORY IS
NOT RELEVANT.
OPTION D: CONJUNCTIVITIS IS NOT A FEATURE OF NIACIN DEFICIENCY.

A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH SYMPTOMS OF DELAYED ADAPTATION TO VISION IN DARK PLACES, GRITTY
SENSATION IN THE EYES, DRY EYES, AND SOFTENING OF THE CORNEA. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DEFICIENCY IN

THE CLINICAL PICTURE OF DELAYED ADAPTATION TO VISION IN DARK PLACES, GRITTY SENSATION IN THE EYES, DRY
EYES, AND SOFTENING OF THE CORNEA IS SUGGESTIVE OF VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY IN THE PATIENT. HENCE

RETINOIC ACID (THE ACTIVE FORM OF VITAMIN A) IS LIKELY TO BE DEFICIENT.
VITAMIN A IS A FAT-SOLUBLE VITAMIN THAT CAN OCCUR AS CAROTENOIDS (MOST COMMON - BETA CAROTENE
FROM PLANT SOURCES) OR RETINOIDS (FROM ANIMAL SOURCES).
3 FORMS OF RETINOIDS ARE:
- RETINAL IS REQUIRED MAINLY FOR NORMAL VISION (PRESENT IN THE VISUAL PIGMENT RHODOPSIN).
- RETINOL IS IMPORTANT FOR THE NORMAL FUNCTIONING OF THE REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM.
- RETINOIC ACID HAS A ROLE IN THE REGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION AND TISSUE DIFFERENTIATION.
OCULAR MANIFESTATIONS OF VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY INCLUDE LOSS OF SENSITIVITY TO GREEN LIGHT (EARLIEST TO
APPEAR), NYCTALOPIA (NIGHT BLINDNESS), XEROPHTHALMIA.
XEROPHTHALMIA INCLUDES CONJUNCTIVAL XEROSIS (DRYNESS) WITH BITOT’S SPOTS (WHITE PATCHES OF
KERATINIZED EPITHELIUM APPEARING ON THE SCLERA), CORNEAL ULCERS, AND KERATOMALACIA (SOFTENING OF
THE CORNEA) THAT LEADS TO CORNEAL SCARRING AND ULTIMATELY, BLINDNESS.
OTHER MANIFESTATIONS: GENERAL IMPAIRMENT OF IMMUNITY, KERATINIZATION OF SKIN (PHRYNODERMA/TOAD
SKIN).

INJECTION SHOULD BE GIVEN IMMEDIATELY ON DIAGNOSIS (DAY 0) AND REPEATED THE FOLLOWING DAY (DAY 1)
AND 14 DAYS LATER.
DIETARY SOURCES OF VITAMIN A ARE LIVER, FISH, EGGS, DARK GREEN, AND DEEPLY COLORED FRUITS AND
VEGETABLES.

YOU ARE CONDUCTING AN EXPERIMENT ON MITOCHONDRIAL RESPIRATION. YOU ADD MALATE/PYRUVATE
AND RESPIRATION IS NORMAL. YOU ADD SUCCINATE AND RESPIRATION IS NORMAL. WHEN YOU ADD
ANOTHER SUBSTANCE IN THE PRESENCE OF PYRUVATE/SUCCINATE AND MALATE, RESPIRATION IS BLOCKED.
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING SUBSTANCES IS MOST LIKELY ADDED?
questions.explanation:
IN THE EXPERIMENT CONDUCTED ON MITOCHONDRIAL RESPIRATION, RESPIRATION WILL BE BLOCKED BY THE
ADDITION OF OLIGOMYCIN, AN ANTIBIOTIC, WHEN ADDED IN THE PRESENCE OF PYRUVATE/ SUCCINATE AND
MALATE. OLIGOMYCIN INHIBITS OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION IN THE MITOCHONDRIA AND HENCE BLOCKS
RESPIRATION.
ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (ETC)/RESPIRATORY CHAIN IS THE FINAL PATHWAY BY WHICH ALL THE ELECTRONS
DERIVED FROM THE OXIDATION OF CARBOHYDRATES, FATTY ACIDS, AND AMINO ACIDS ARE DIRECTED TOWARDS THE
FINAL REACTION WITH OXYGEN, TO FORM WATER AND ADENOSINE TRIPHOSPHATE (ATP).
THE CHEMIOSMOTIC THEORY STATES THAT THE FLOW OF ELECTRONS THROUGH THE RESPIRATORY CHAIN GENERATES
A PROTON MOTIVE FORCE. THIS FORCE DRIVES THE FORMATION OF ATP BY THE PROCESS OF OXIDATIVE
PHOSPHORYLATION.
IN THE GIVEN EXPERIMENT, MALATE AND PYRUVATE ARE ELECTRON DONORS (NADH) AT COMPLEX I OF THE
ETC, AND SUCCINATE IS THE ELECTRON DONOR (FADH2) AT COMPLEX II. NORMAL RESPIRATION IS OBSERVED
ON THE ADDITION OF SUBSTANCES AT BOTH COMPLEXES I AND II I.E., BOTH OXYGEN CONSUMPTION AND ATP
SYNTHESIS FROM ADP (ADENOSINE DIPHOSPHATE) TAKE PLACE.
OLIGOMYCIN IS A COMPETITIVE INHIBITOR OF THE FO (OLIGOMYCIN-SENSITIVE) COMPLEX OF ATP SYNTHASE
(COMPLEX V) AND BLOCKS OXIDATION AND PHOSPHORYLATION BY STOPPING THE FLOW OF PROTONS THROUGH
THE ATP SYNTHASE ENZYME COMPLEX. HENCE THE ADDITION OF OLIGOMYCIN WILL INHIBIT COMPLEX V AND
STOP RESPIRATION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTIONS A AND B: ROTENONE (OPTION A) IF ADDED, WILL INHIBIT COMPLEX I. ELECTRON TRANSFER BEFORE
COMPLEX I WILL BE BLOCKED BUT NOT AFTER. HENCE, NORMAL RESPIRATION WILL OCCUR. SIMILARLY, ANTIMYCIN
A (OPTION B) INHIBITS COMPLEX III, AND ELECTRON TRANSFER PRIOR TO COMPLEX III WILL BE BLOCKED AND
830
NOT AFTER. HENCE, RESPIRATION WILL NOT BE COMPLETELY HINDERED.
OPTION C: 2,4-DINITROPHENOL (DNP) IS AN UNCOUPLER THAT DISSOCIATES OXIDATION IN THE RESPIRATORY
CHAIN FROM PHOSPHORYLATION. HENCE, RESPIRATION CONTINUES WITHOUT ATP SYNTHESIS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH TENDON XANTHOMAS. HIS LIPID PROFILE SHOWED SERUM CHOLESTEROL LEVELS
TO BE 283 MG/DL AND SERUM LDL TO BE 202 MG/DL. HE WAS STARTED ON LOVASTATIN. WHAT IS THE
LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION WITH TENDON XANTHOMAS AND ELEVATED SERUM LDL (LOW-DENSITY
LIPOPROTEIN) AND ELEVATED SERUM CHOLESTEROL POINTS TO A DIAGNOSIS OF FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA
(FH).
FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA (TYPE IIA HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA) IS AN INHERITED DISORDER DUE TO
DEFECTS IN LDL RECEPTORS. THIS DEFECT CAUSES A DECREASE IN THE UPTAKE OF LDL AND CHOLESTEROL. AS A
RESULT, THE BLOOD LEVELS OF BOTH LDL AND CHOLESTEROL ARE ELEVATED. SUCH PATIENTS ARE AT INCREASED
RISK TO DEVELOP ATHEROSCLEROSIS AND CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE.
FEATURES OF FH:
- PAINFUL POLYARTHRITIS AND TENDINITIS ARE COMMON.
- PHYSICAL FINDINGS SEEN ARE CORNEAL ARCUS AND TENDON XANTHOMAS OVER ACHILLES TENDON AND THE
DORSUM OF HANDS. XANTHOMAS ARE TUMOROUS MASSES PRODUCED BY FOAMY CELL CLUSTERS (LIPID-LADEN
MACROPHAGES) FOUND IN THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE OF THE SKIN AND IN TENDONS.
DIAGNOSIS IS DONE CLINICALLY BASED ON HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA WITH
- LDL > 190 MG/DL,
- FAMILY HISTORY OF HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA AND/OR
- PREMATURE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE.
TREATMENT INCLUDES LIFESTYLE CHANGES, RESTRICTION OF A FATTY DIET, AND PHARMACOTHERAPY WITH STATINS
IN HETEROZYGOUS FH PATIENTS.
RECENT DRUGS FOR SPECIFIC TREATMENT OF HOMOZYGOUS FH ARE:
- LOMITAPIDE, A MICROSOMAL TRIGLYCERIDE TRANSFER PROTEIN (MTP) INHIBITOR, AND
- MIPOMERSEN, AN ANTISENSE OLIGONUCLEOTIDE AGAINST APOB.
831
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS ACHILLES TENDON XANTHOMA AND A PLAIN LATERAL RADIOGRAPH OF BOTH ANKLES
SHOWING BILATERAL SYMMETRICAL SWELLINGS (ARROWS) SUPERIOR TO THE CALCANEUM RESPECTIVELY.
OTHER OPTIONS
OPTION B: TANGIER’S DISEASE IS A HYPOLIPOPROTEINEMIA CAUSED BY A MUTATION OF THE ABCA1 GENE.
ENLARGED ORANGE TONSILS ARE PATHOGNOMONIC. LOW HDL LEVELS ARE SEEN. THERE IS AN INCREASED RISK
FOR ATHEROSCLEROSIS.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS ENLARGED YELLOW-ORANGE COLORED TONSILS IN TANGIER'S DISEASE.
832
OPTION C: LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE (LPL) DEFICIENCY CAUSES TYPE I HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA DUE TO DEFECTS IN
LPL OR APO C-II. ERUPTIVE XANTHOMAS ARE SEEN. CHYLOMICRONS AND VLDL ARE ELEVATED. LDL AND
HDL ARE LOW. THERE IS NO RISK FOR CORONARY DISEASE.
OPTION D: FAMILIAL HYPERCHYLOMICRONEMIA SYNDROME IS CAUSED DUE TO EITHER LPL
DEFICIENCY, APOC-II DEFICIENCY, APOA-V DEFICIENCY, OR GPIHBP1 MUTATION. CLINICALLY, PATIENTS
PRESENT WITH RECURRENT EPISODES OF SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN DUE TO ACUTE PANCREATITIS. THE RETINAL
BLOOD VESSELS MAY BE OPALESCENT AND ARE CALLED LIPEMIA RETINALIS. INCREASED LEVELS OF TRIGLYCERIDES
(MOSTLY >1000 MG/DL) IS SEEN. THE RISK OF PREMATURE CORONARY HEART DISEASE IS LOW.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING GLYCOSAMINOGLYCANS (GAGS) ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR CORNEAL TRANSPARENCY?
questions.explanation:
THE GLYCOSAMINOGLYCAN (GAG) RESPONSIBLE FOR CORNEAL TRANSPARENCY IS KERATAN SULFATE.
GLYCOSAMINOGLYCANS OR MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDES ARE COMPLEX CARBOHYDRATES MADE UP OF AMINO SUGARS
AND URONIC ACIDS. THEY MAY BE ATTACHED TO A PROTEIN MOLECULE TO FORM A PROTEOGLYCAN.
KERATAN SULFATE IS A MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDE THAT DOES NOT CONTAIN URONIC ACID. IT IS CONSTITUTED BY
REPEATING DISACCHARIDE UNITS OF N-ACETYL GLUCOSAMINE AND GALACTOSE.
KERATAN SULFATE IS PRESENT BETWEEN THE COLLAGEN FIBRILS IN THE CORNEA AND PLAYS A MAJOR ROLE IN
CORNEAL TRANSPARENCY.
2 TYPES OF KERATAN SULFATE ARE SEEN:
- KERATAN SULFATE I IS PRESENT IN THE CORNEA.
- KERATAN SULFATE II IS MAINLY PRESENT IN THE CARTILAGE.
KERATIN SULFATE I AND II DIFFER IN THEIR LINKAGE TO THE CORE PROTEINS. KERATAN SULFATE I LINKS TO A CORE
PROTEIN L-ASPARAGINE VIA N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE AND KERATAN SULFATE II TO L-SERINE (OR L-THREONINE)
VIA N-ACETYLGALACTOSAMINE.
THE CHEMICAL STRUCTURE OF KERATAN SULFATE IS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE BELOW.
833
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: IN CHONDROITIN SULFATES (CHONDROITIN 4-SULFATE & CHONDROITIN 6-SULFATE), THE
REPEATING DISACCHARIDE UNITS ARE GLUCURONIC ACID AND N-ACETYLGALACTOSAMINE. THEY MAINTAIN THE
STRUCTURE OF THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) AND ARE LOCATED IN ENDOCHONDRAL BONE AND CARTILAGE.
THEY ARE ALSO FOUND IN THE ECM OF THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. THEY ACT AS SIGNALING MOLECULES IN
THE PREVENTION OF THE REPAIR OF NERVE ENDINGS AFTER INJURY.
OPTION C: HEPARAN SULFATE IS FOUND ON MANY EXTRACELLULAR CELL SURFACES AND CONTAINS GLUCOSAMINE
WITH FEWER N-SULFATES THAN HEPARIN. THE PREDOMINANT URONIC ACID IS D-GLUCURONIC ACID. IN THE
PLASMA MEMBRANE OF CELLS, THEY ACT AS RECEPTORS AND MEDIATE CELL GROWTH AND CELL-CELL
COMMUNICATION. IT IS ALSO FOUND IN THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE OF THE KIDNEY ALONG WITH TYPE IV
COLLAGEN AND LAMININ, WHERE IT DETERMINES THE CHARGE SELECTIVENESS OF GLOMERULAR FILTRATION.
OPTION D: HYALURONIC ACID IS PRESENT IN SYNOVIAL FLUID. IT IS ALSO FOUND IN SKIN, BONE, CARTILAGE,
VITREOUS HUMOR, AND EMBRYONIC TISSUES. IT CONTAINS REPEATING UNITS OF N ACETYL GLUCOSAMINE AND
GLUCURONIC ACID. IT PLAYS A ROLE IN MORPHOGENESIS AND WOUND REPAIR. THE HIGH CONCENTRATIONS OF
HYALURONIC ACID ALONG WITH CHONDROITIN SULFATES IN CARTILAGE CONTRIBUTE TO ITS COMPRESSIBILITY.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PERSON WHO HAD DINNER AT 8 PM THE PREVIOUS NIGHT, TESTED HIS BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS AT 7 AM
THE NEXT MORNING. WHAT IS THE SOURCE OF BLOOD GLUCOSE IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THE SOURCE OF BLOOD GLUCOSE IN A PERSON FASTING OVERNIGHT FOR 11 HOURS (8 PM TO 7 AM) IS HEPATIC
GLYCOGENOLYSIS.
FIRST STAGE OF FASTING: THE FASTING STATE BEGINS TWO TO FOUR HOURS AFTER THE ABSORPTIVE/WELL-FED STATE.
IN EARLY FASTING I.E; 4-18 HOURS AFTER THE WELL-FED STATE, THE BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVEL IS MAINTAINED BY
HEPATIC GLYCOGENOLYSIS. THE GLYCOGEN STORES ARE SUFFICIENT FOR AROUND 18 HOURS AFTER A MEAL
FOLLOWING WHICH THEY START TO DEPLETE. SO THE SOURCE OF BLOOD GLUCOSE IN A PERSON FASTING FOR 11
HOURS WILL BE LIVER GLYCOGENOLYSIS.
SECOND STAGE OF FASTING: GLUCONEOGENESIS BEGINS 4–6 HOURS AFTER THE LAST MEAL BUT BECOMES FULLY
ACTIVE ONLY AFTER STORES OF LIVER GLYCOGEN ARE DEPLETED (AFTER 18 HOURS). THEY CAN SERVE AS A SOURCE
834
OF GLUCOSE FOR UP TO 2 DAYS.
SUBSTRATES FOR GLUCONEOGENESIS ARE:
- GLUCOGENIC AMINO ACIDS ( MAINLY ALANINE) FROM THE MUSCLE AND
- GLYCEROL FROM ADIPOSE TISSUE
DURING FASTING, THE GLUCOGENIC AMINO ACIDS ARE TRANSPORTED TO THE LIVER, TRANSAMINATED INTO
PYRUVATE, AND CONVERTED TO GLUCOSE.
THIRD STAGE OF FASTING:
- LIPOLYSIS OCCURS IN THE ADIPOSE TISSUE DUE TO THE ACTIVITY OF HORMONE-SENSITIVE LIPASE, STIMULATED
BY INCREASED GLUCAGON:INSULIN RATIO.
- FREE FATTY ACIDS ARE THE SOURCE OF ENERGY IN THIS STAGE AND NOT GLUCOSE. TRIACYLGLYCEROLS WILL BE
HYDROLYZED TO FATTY ACIDS AND GLYCEROL.
- BETA OXIDATION OF FATTY ACIDS TAKES PLACE WHICH PROVIDES ACETYL COA.
- IN PROLONGED STARVATION (>3 DAYS), ACETYL COA IS CONVERTED TO KETONE BODIES IN THE LIVER WHICH
WILL ACT AS THE MAIN FUEL SOURCE FOR SKELETAL AND HEART MUSCLE AND CAN MEET UP TO 20% OF THE
BRAIN’S ENERGY NEEDS.
FINAL STAGE OF FASTING: AFTER SEVERAL WEEKS OF STARVATION, KETONE BODY SYNTHESIS WILL NOT TAKE PLACE
DUE TO DEPLETED TRIACYLGLYCEROL STORES. PROTEINS REMAIN THE ONLY SOURCE OF FUEL. PROTEIN DEGRADATION
INCREASES, AND DEATH RESULTS FROM A LOSS OF HEART, LIVER, OR KIDNEY FUNCTION.
ROLE OF INSULIN AND GLUCAGON:
WHEN BLOOD GLUCOSE FALLS DURING FASTING, THERE IS INCREASED SECRETION OF GLUCAGON AND DECREASED
RELEASE OF INSULIN. HENCE GLUCAGON:INSULIN RATIO IS INCREASED.
EFFECTS OF INCREASED GLUCAGON:INSULIN RATIO ON ENZYMES OF GLYCOGENOLYSIS AND GLUCONEOGENESIS:
- IT ACTIVATES GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE, THE KEY ENZYME OF GLYCOGENOLYSIS, AND DEACTIVATES GLYCOGEN
SYNTHASE. THIS CAUSES A RAPID MOBILIZATION OF LIVER GLYCOGEN STORES TO BE UTILIZED AS FUEL.
- IT FAVORS THE SYNTHESIS OF GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATASE WHICH CONVERTS GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE TO GLUCOSE.
THE RESULTING GLUCOSE IS USED BY RED BLOOD CELLS (LACK MITOCHONDRIA) AND THE BRAIN AS THEY ARE
LARGELY DEPENDANT ON GLUCOSE IN THE FASTING STATE.
- PHOSPHOENOL PYRUVATE CARBOXYKINASE AND FRUCTOSE-1, 6-BISPHOSPHATASE ARE INDUCED, LEADING TO
INCREASED GLUCONEOGENESIS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WHO HAS BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH MULTIPLE GASTROINTESTINAL POLYPS AND CARCINOMA, WITH
A POSITIVE FAMILY HISTORY/HISTORY OF HEREDITARY NON-POLYPOSIS COLON CARCINOMA HAS A DEFECT IN
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING?
questions.explanation:
MISMATCH REPAIR WILL BE DEFECTIVE IN A PATIENT WITH MULTIPLE GASTROINTESTINAL POLYPS AND
CARCINOMA, WITH A POSITIVE FAMILY HISTORY/HISTORY OF HEREDITARY NON-POLYPOSIS COLON CARCINOMA
(HNPCC)
MISMATCH REPAIR IS A DNA REPAIR MECHANISM THAT CORRECTS SINGLE-NUCLEOTIDE MISMATCHES,
INSERTIONS, AND DELETIONS INTRODUCED BY THE DNA POLYMERASE DURING DNA REPLICATION.
HNPCC OR LYNCH SYNDROME IS AN AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT GENETIC CONDITION. IT OCCURS DUE TO DEFECTS
IN DNA MISMATCH REPAIR GENES LIKE MLH1 AND MSH2. THE GENOMES OF THESE PATIENTS SHOW
MICROSATELLITE INSTABILITY. HNPCC IS ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGH RISK OF COLON CANCER. IT MAY ALSO BE
ASSOCIATED WITH A RISK OF DEVELOPING CARCINOMAS OF THE ENDOMETRIUM, STOMACH, SMALL BOWEL, OVARY,
PANCREAS, AND TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA OF THE URETER AND RENAL PELVIS.
THE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR HNPCC ARE REFERRED TO AS THE AMSTERDAM CRITERIA OR THE 3-2-1-0 RULE. IT
INCLUDES:
- THREE OR MORE RELATIVES WITH HNPCC-ASSOCIATED CANCER (COLORECTAL CANCER, ENDOMETRIAL CANCER,
CANCER OF THE SMALL BOWEL, URETER, OR RENAL PELVIS), ONE OF WHOM IS A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE OF THE
OTHER TWO.
- AT LEAST TWO SUCCESSIVE GENERATIONS AFFECTED
- AT LEAST ONE CASE DIAGNOSED BEFORE AGE 50 YEARS
- FAMILIAL ADENOMATOUS POLYPOSIS EXCLUDED
- TUMORS VERIFIED BY PATHOLOGIC EXAMINATION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: PATIENTS WITH XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM HAVE A DEFECT IN THE NUCLEOTIDE EXCISION REPAIR
PATHWAY.
OPTION C: DEFECT IN BASE EXCISION REPAIR PATHWAY IS SEEN IN PATIENTS WITH MUTYH-ASSOCIATED
POLYPOSIS.
OPTION D: SICKLE CELL DISEASE AND BETA-THALASSEMIA ARE EXAMPLES OF DISEASES SEEN IN PATIENTS WITH
POINT MUTATIONS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
THE ENZYMES THAT CONVERT PYRUVATE TO ACETYL COA ARE GIVEN IN THE DIAGRAM. WHAT ARE THE
ENZYMES MARKED AS E1 AND E2 RESPECTIVELY?
questions.explanation:
E1 IS PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE AND E2 IS DIHYDROLIPOYL TRANSACETYLASE IN THE IMAGE SHOWING
OXIDATIVE DECARBOXYLATION OF PYRUVATE. THIS IS CATALYZED BY THE PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (PDH)
COMPLEX WHERE E1, E2, AND E3 ARE THE THREE ENZYME COMPONENTS OF THE COMPLEX.
THE PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (PDH) COMPLEX IS A MULTIENZYME COMPLEX THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH THE
INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE. IT CATALYZES THE OXIDATIVE DECARBOXYLATION OF PYRUVATE TO
ACETYL-COA WHICH ENTERS THE CITRIC ACID/KREB’S CYCLE.
STEPS OF PYRUVATE DECARBOXYLATION:
- PYRUVATE IS TRANSPORTED INTO THE MITOCHONDRIA BY A PROTON SYMPORTER.
837
- PYRUVATE IS DECARBOXYLATED BY PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (E1). TPP IS REQUIRED FOR THIS STEP. THE
DECARBOXYLATED PYRUVATE REMAINS BOUND TO THE ENZYME, AS HYDROXYETHYL THIAMINE PYROPHOSPHATE.
- THE HYDROXYETHYL GROUP IS OXIDIZED TO FORM AN ACETYL GROUP. IT IS THEN TRANSFERRED FROM TPP TO
LIPOAMIDE TO FORM ACETYL LIPOAMIDE. THIS STEP IS CATALYZED BY DIHYDROLIPOYL TRANSACETYLASE (E2).
- ACETYL LIPOAMIDE REACTS WITH COENZYME A TO FORM ACETYL-COA AND REDUCED LIPOAMIDE.
- THE REDUCED LIPOAMIDE IS REOXIDIZED BY FAD-DEPENDENT DIHYDROLIPOYL DEHYDROGENASE (E3).
THE OVERALL REACTION IS : PYRUVATE + NAD+ + COA → ACETYL-COA + NADH + H+ + CO2

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A YOUNG GIRL PRESENTED TO THE OPD FOR EXAMINATION. SHE IS TALL AND THIN WITH SLENDER FINGERS,
AND DISLOCATED LENSES. WORKUP REVEALED CYSTATHIONINE BETA-SYNTHASE DEFICIENCY. WHICH AMINO
ACID SUPPLEMENT IS REQUIRED IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PICTURE OF A TALL AND THIN YOUNG GIRL WITH SLENDER FINGERS, DISLOCATED LENSES, AND
CYSTATHIONINE BETA-SYNTHASE DEFICIENCY IS SUGGESTIVE OF CLASSIC HOMOCYSTINURIA. THE AMINO ACID
SUPPLEMENT REQUIRED IN THIS SCENARIO IS CYSTEINE.
CLASSIC HOMOCYSTINURIA IS A METABOLIC DISORDER OF METHIONINE METABOLISM, DUE TO CYSTATHIONINE
BETA-SYNTHASE DEFICIENCY. IT IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE CONDITION.
CYSTATHIONINE BETA-SYNTHASE IS A PYRIDOXAL PHOSPHATE-DEPENDENT ENZYME THAT CONDENSES
HOMOCYSTEINE WITH SERINE TO FORM CYSTATHIONINE. THE ABSENCE OF THIS ENZYME WILL CAUSE CYSTEINE
DEFICIENCY, HENCE CYSTEINE NEEDS TO BE SUPPLEMENTED IN THE DIET.
CLINICAL FEATURES:
- AFFECTED CHILDREN ARE INITIALLY ASYMPTOMATIC.
- ECTOPIA LENTIS (SUBLUXATION OF THE LENS) IS SEEN FIRST, AFTER 3 YEARS OF AGE.
- INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY AND PSYCHIATRIC AND BEHAVIORAL DISORDERS.
- THROMBOEMBOLIC EPISODES.
- SKELETAL ABNORMALITIES RESEMBLING THOSE OF MARFAN SYNDROME: THEY ARE TALL AND THIN WITH
ELONGATED LIMBS AND ARACHNODACTYLY (SLENDER FINGERS).
ELEVATIONS OF BOTH METHIONINE AND HOMOCYSTEINE IN BODY FLUIDS ARE THE DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY
FINDINGS. THE DIAGNOSIS IS ESTABLISHED BY MOLECULAR ANALYSIS OF CYSTATHIONINE β-SYNTHASE (CBS) OR
BY ASSAY OF THE ENZYME IN CULTURED FIBROBLASTS, PHYTOHEMAGGLUTININ-STIMULATED LYMPHOCYTES, OR
LIVER BIOPSY SPECIMENS. TREATMENT INCLUDES RESTRICTION OF METHIONINE INTAKE AND SUPPLEMENTATION
WITH CYSTEINE, BETAINE, VITAMINS B6, B12, AND FOLATE.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS ARACHNODACTYLY.
839
METHIONINE SUPPLEMENTATION IS REQUIRED IN NON-CLASSICAL HOMOCYSTINURIA. IT IS DUE TO IMPAIRED
RE-METHYLATION OF HOMOCYSTEINE TO METHIONINE. THIS CAN BE CAUSED BY DEFECTIVE METHIONINE
SYNTHASE OR REDUCED AVAILABILITY OF TWO ESSENTIAL COFACTORS, 5-METHYLTETRAHYDROFOLATE, AND
METHYLCOBALAMIN.
ELEVATED HOMOCYSTEINE LEVELS WITH LOW LEVELS OF METHIONINE WILL BE SEEN. TREATMENT INCLUDES
METHIONINE SUPPLEMENTATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF METHYL FOLATE, HYDROXOCOBALAMIN, AND
BETAINE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH JOINT PAIN AND ON EVALUATION, URINE TURNS BLACK ON STANDING. WHAT IS
THE LIKELY ENZYME DEFICIENCY?
questions.explanation:
THE URINE TURNING BLACK IN COLOR, ON EXPOSURE TO AIR, ALONG WITH JOINT PAIN IS SUGGESTIVE OF
ALKAPTONURIA. IT OCCURS DUE TO THE DEFECT IN THE HOMOGENTISIC ACID 1, 2 - DIOXYGENASE ENZYME.
ALKAPTONURIA IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE DISORDER OF TYROSINE METABOLISM, THAT DEVELOPS DUE TO THE
DEFECT IN HOMOGENTISATE OXIDASE/HOMOGENTISIC ACID 1, 2 - DIOXYGENASE, WHICH OXIDIZES
HOMOGENTISATE TO MALEYLACETOACETATE. THE DEFECT IN THIS ENZYME LEADS TO THE ACCUMULATION OF
HOMOGENTISATE, WHICH IS THEN EXCRETED IN THE URINE.
ALKAPTONURIA IS CHARACTERIZED BY HOMOGENTISIC ACIDURIA, OCHRONOSIS, AND ARTHROPATHY (JOINT PAIN).
HOMOGENTISIC ACIDURIA IS THE BLACK DISCOLORATION OF URINE ON PROLONGED EXPOSURE TO AIR CAUSED DUE
TO OXIDATION OF THE EXCRETED HOMOGENTISATE.
OCHRONOSIS IS THE ACCUMULATION OF OXIDIZED HOMOGENTISIC ACID PIGMENT (ALKAPTONE BODIES) IN
CONNECTIVE TISSUES LEADING TO BLUISH-BLACK DISCOLORATION OF TISSUES MOSTLY INVOLVING EAR CARTILAGE,
OCULAR TISSUE, THE SKIN OF THE EYELIDS, FOREHEAD, CHEEKS, AND HANDS, NAIL BEDS, AND INTERVERTEBRAL
DISCS. THE COMPOUND THAT ACCUMULATES IN THE TISSUES IN OCHRONOSIS IS BENZOQUINONE ACETATE.
PAINFUL ARTHRITIS (ARTHROPATHY) MAY BE SEEN FROM THE FOURTH OR FIFTH DECADE.
DIAGNOSIS: BLACKISH DISCOLORATION OF URINE ON STANDING IS DIAGNOSTIC OF ALKAPTONURIA (SHOWN
BELOW). THE FERRIC CHLORIDE TEST WILL BE POSITIVE.
840
THE IMAGE FURTHER BELOW SHOWS OCHRONOSIS.
TREATMENT: NO SPECIFIC TREATMENT IS REQUIRED. SYMPTOMATIC TREATMENT WITH ANALGESICS, SPINAL
SURGERY, AND ARTHROPLASTY ALONG WITH ASCORBIC ACID AND PROTEIN RESTRICTION CAN BE
CONSIDERED. NITISINONE (P-HYDROXYPHENYLPYRUVIC ACID (PHPPA) OXIDASE INHIBITOR) REDUCES URINARY
EXCRETION OF HOMOGENTISIC ACID.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: TYROSINE TRANSAMINASE DEFICIENCY CAUSES TYPE II TYROSINEMIA (RICHNER-HANHART
SYNDROME). PATIENTS PRESENT WITH PAINFUL CORNEAL EROSIONS WITH PHOTOPHOBIA, LEARNING DISABILITY,
AND PALMOPLANTAR KERATOSIS.
OPTION C: FUMARYLACETOACETATE HYDROLASE DEFICIENCY CAUSES TYPE I TYROSINEMIA (TYROSINOSIS).
PATIENTS GENERALLY PRESENT WITH FAILURE TO THRIVE, NEUROPATHY, BOILED-CABBAGE URINE, AND LIVER
FAILURE SECONDARY TO CIRRHOSIS.
841
OPTION D: 4-HYDROXY-PHENYL PYRUVATE DIOXYGENASE DEFICIENCY CAUSES TYPE III TYROSINEMIA
(NEONATAL TYROSINEMIA). PATIENTS MIGHT RARELY HAVE A MENTAL DISABILITY. THE LIVER FUNCTION IS
GENERALLY NORMAL.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A 5-YEAR-OLD BOY PRESENTED WITH EASY FATIGABILITY, IRRITABILITY AND INABILITY TO CONCENTRATE. LABS
REVEALED THE FOLLOWING FINDINGS A AND B (LIGHT AND OIL IMMERSION RESPECTIVELY) ON THE BONE
MARROW ASPIRATION. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE MOST LIKELY ENZYME DEFICIENT IN THIS
CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF A CHILD WITH EASY FATIGUABILITY, IRRITABILITY, AND INABILITY TO
CONCENTRATE WITH THE IMAGES SHOWING A CRUMPLED TISSUE PAPER APPEARANCE(GAUCHER'S CELL) IS
SUGGESTIVE OF GAUCHER'S DISEASE. THE DEFICIENT ENZYME IS GLUCOCEREBROSIDASE (ALSO KNOWN AS
BETA-GLUCOSIDASE). I
GAUCHER'S DISEASE IS AN INBORN ERROR OF METABOLISM CAUSED DUE TO A DEFICIENCY OF BETA
GLUCOCEREBROSIDASE. IT IS THE MOST COMMON LYSOSOMAL STORAGE DISORDER AND THE MODE OF
INHERITANCE IS AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE. THERE IS AN ACCUMULATION OF LIPID-LADEN MACROPHAGES IN THE
SPLEEN, LIVER, AND OTHER TISSUES.
THERE ARE THREE CLINICAL SUBTYPES - TYPE I (CHRONIC NON-NEURONOPATHIC), TYPE II (ACUTE
NEURONOPATHIC), AND TYPE III (INTERMEDIATE). CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE ANEMIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA,
HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY, AND NEUROLOGICAL FEATURES DEPENDING ON THE SUBTYPE.
GAUCHER'S CELLS - THESE ARE FORMED AS A RESULT OF THE ACCUMULATION OF MASSIVE AMOUNTS OF
GLUCOCEREBROSIDES WITHIN THE PHAGOCYTES. THE CELLS HAVE A FIBRILLARY CYTOPLASM AND GIVE A CRUMPLED
TISSUE PAPER APPEARANCE.
OPTION A: DEFICIENCY OF BETA-HEXOSAMINIDASE A IS SEEN IN TAY-SACHS DISEASE. THE DEFICIENCY OF
BETA-HEXOSAMINIDASE A AND B CAUSES SANDHOFF'S DISEASE. CLINICAL FEATURES ARE SEIZURES,
MACROCEPHALY, AND HYPERACUSIS.
OPTION C: DEFICIENCY OF SPHINGOMYELINASE LEADS TO NIEMANN-PICK DISEASE. IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY
THE PRESENCE OF FOAM CELLS IN THE BONE MARROW. THERE MAY BE PULMONARY INFILTRATES LEADING TO LUNG
FAILURE.
842
OPTION D: DEFICIENCY OF N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINIDASE LEADS TO SANFILLIPO'S DISEASE. IT IS A TYPE OF
MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDOSIS (MPS - III). THERE IS AN ACCUMULATION OF HEPARAN SULFATE LEADING TO SEVERE
COGNITIVE DEGENERATION.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A FARMER PRESENTED WITH LOOSE STOOLS AND RASHES OVER THE SUN-EXPOSED AREAS. CAREFUL DIET
HISTORY REVEALS A DIET RICH IN MAIZE. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING DEFICIENCIES WOULD YOU SUSPECT?
options:
BIOTIN
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
HISTORY OF A MAIZE-RICH DIET ALONG WITH LOOSE STOOLS AND RASHES OVER THE SUN-EXPOSED AREAS IS
SUGGESTIVE OF NIACIN/VITAMIN B3 DEFICIENCY.
NIACIN DEFICIENCY CAUSES PELLAGRA, FOUND MOSTLY AMONG PEOPLE EATING CORN/MAIZE-BASED DIETS,
WHICH IS LOW IN NIACIN AND TRYPTOPHAN. EXCESS LEUCINE IN JOWAR AND MAIZE DISRUPTS THE CONVERSION
OF TRYPTOPHAN TO NIACIN.
NIACIN CAN BE SYNTHESIZED IN THE BODY FROM TRYPTOPHAN. TWO COMPOUNDS- NICOTINIC ACID, AND
NICOTINAMIDE HAVE THE BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY OF NIACIN. THE NICOTINAMIDE RING OF THE COENZYMES NAD (
NICOTINAMIDE ADENINE DINUCLEOTIDE) AND NADP (NICOTINAMIDE ADENINE DINUCLEOTIDE PHOSPHATE)
PARTICIPATE IN OXIDATION/REDUCTION REACTIONS.
THE INITIAL SYMPTOMS OF PELLAGRA INCLUDE LOSS OF APPETITE, GENERALIZED WEAKNESS, IRRITABILITY,
ABDOMINAL PAIN, AND VOMITING. THIS IS FOLLOWED BY BRIGHT RED GLOSSITIS AND A CHARACTERISTIC
PIGMENTED, SCALY SKIN RASH IN SUN-EXPOSED AREAS. THIS RASH IS KNOWN AS CASAL’S NECKLACE WHEN IT
FORMS A RING AROUND THE NECK.
THE 4DS OF PELLAGRA:
- DIARRHEA
- DERMATITIS
- DEMENTIA, LEADING TO
- DEATH
IT IS DIAGNOSED BY MEASURING URINARY LEVELS OF 2-METHYL NICOTINAMIDE AND 2-PYRIDONE.
IT IS TREATED BY ORAL SUPPLEMENTATION OF 100–200 MG OF NICOTINAMIDE OR NICOTINIC ACID THREE TIMES
DAILY FOR 5 DAYS.
CASAL’S NECKLACE FINDING IN NIACIN DEFICIENCY
843
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: DIETARY PYRIDOXINE DEFICIENCY (VITAMIN B6) IS RARE BUT HAS BEEN OBSERVED IN ALCOHOLICS,
NEWBORN INFANTS FORMULAS LOW IN VITAMIN B6, AND WOMEN TAKING ORAL CONTRACEPTIVES. ISONIAZID, AN
ANTI-TB DRUG, LEADS TO PYRIDOXINE DEFICIENCY RESULTING IN PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY. HENCE PYRIDOXINE
SUPPLEMENTATION IS INCLUDED IN ATT REGIMENS.
OPTION C: THIAMINE DEFICIENCY (VITAMIN B1) CAN MANIFEST AS WET BERIBERI (CVS FEATURES LIKE HEART
FAILURE AND EDEMA) OR SHOSHIN BERIBERI, AN ACUTE AND FULMINANT FORM OF WET BERIBERI, DRY BERIBERI
(PERIPHERAL NEURITIS), OR AS WERNICKE ENCEPHALOPATHY WITH KORSAKOFF PSYCHOSIS (IN
ALCOHOLICS). DIETARY DEFICIENCY OF THIAMINE INHIBITS PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE. CHRONIC ALCOHOLICS
MAY DEVELOP POTENTIALLY FATAL PYRUVIC AND LACTIC ACIDOSIS.
OPTION D: DIETARY BIOTIN DEFICIENCY IS UNKNOWN BUT RARELY, DERMATITIS, GLOSSITIS, LOSS OF APPETITE,
AND NAUSEA MAY OCCUR AFTER CONSUMPTION OF LARGE AMOUNTS OF UNCOOKED EGG WHITE, WHICH CONTAINS
THE PROTEIN AVIDIN. IT BINDS BIOTIN AND MAKES IT UNAVAILABLE FOR ABSORPTION.
NOTE: A SIMILAR IMAGE-BASED QUESTION ON VITAMIN B3 DEFICIENCY WAS PREVIOUSLY ASKED IN NEET PG
2020. VITAMIN DEFICIENCIES ARE A HIGH-YIELD TOPIC AND ARE REPEATEDLY TESTED EVERY YEAR.
844

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
WHICH IS THE CORRECT SEQUENCE OF STEPS IN THE ISOLATION OF DESIRABLE PROTEIN USING RECOMBINANT
DNA TECHNOLOGY?
questions.explanation:
THE CORRECT SEQUENCE OF ISOLATION OF DESIRABLE PROTEIN IN RECOMBINANT DNA TECHNOLOGY IS 2, 1, 3, 5,
4.
I) INCORPORATION OF GENES INTO BACTERIA: THE GENE NEEDED TO PRODUCE THE DESIRED PROTEINS IS TO BE
INCORPORATED INTO THE BACTERIA. THIS IS DONE USING CLONING VECTORS LIKE BACTERIAL PLASMIDS, PHAGES,
OR COSMIDS. THE DNA OF INTEREST IS LIGATED INTO THE VECTOR DNA AND IS CALLED RECOMBINANT DNA.
THIS VECTOR IS THEN INSERTED INTO A COMPETENT HOST CELL (EG: E.COLI BACTERIA) WHERE IT IS REPLICATED.
II) EXPRESSION OF PROTEIN AND LYSIS OF BACTERIAL CELL: AFTER INCORPORATION OF RECOMBINANT DNA,
BACTERIA EXPRESS THE INSERTED GENE AND PRODUCE THE DESIRED PROTEIN ON A LARGE SCALE ALONG WITH
OTHER INDIGENOUS BACTERIAL PROTEINS. TO RELEASE THESE PROTEINS BACTERIAL CELL IS LYSED.
III) SDS-PAGE (SODIUM DODECYL SULFATE-POLYACRYLAMIDE GEL ELECTROPHORESIS): IT IS THE MOST WIDELY
USED METHOD FOR DETERMINING THE PURITY OF A PROTEIN. AFTER THE PROTEINS ARE RELEASED, TO
SEPARATE THE DESIRABLE PROTEIN, WE SUBJECT IT TO SDS-PAGE. IT SEPARATES PROTEINS BASED ON
MOLECULAR WEIGHT.
IV) HYBRIDIZATION AND BLOTTING: IT IS DONE TO CONFIRM THAT THE ISOLATED PROTEIN IS THE DESIRED
PROTEIN. IT IS DONE USING WESTERN BLOTTING TECHNIQUES ON NITROCELLULOSE PAPER.
V) PROTEIN ELUTION - EXTRACTION OF THE PRODUCED PROTEIN.
THE PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS OF RECOMBINANT DNA TECHNOLOGY INCLUDE:
- GENE MAPPING USING TECHNIQUES SUCH AS FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH).
- PRODUCING PROTEINS SUCH AS:
854
- INTERFERONS, TPA (TISSUE PLASMINOGEN ACTIVATOR)
- INSULIN, GROWTH HORMONE
- HEPATITIS B VACCINE
- MOLECULAR ANALYSIS OF DISEASE, TO DETECT GENE VARIATIONS AND MUTATIONS.
- RESTRICTION FRAGMENT LENGTH POLYMORPHISM (RFLP) AND SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISM (SNP)
- MICROSATELLITE DNA POLYMORPHISMS
- GENE THERAPY AND BONE MARROW TRANSPLANTATION

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING TECHNIQUES IS USED TO DETECT DNA-PROTEIN INTERACTION?
questions.explanation:
THE TECHNIQUE USED TO DETECT DNA-PROTEIN INTERACTION IS DNA FOOTPRINTING.
THE PARTS OF DNA THAT ARE PROTEIN-BOUND (EG: RNA POLYMERASE BOUND TO THE PROMOTER REGION OF
DNA) ARE RESISTANT TO DIGESTION BY NUCLEASE ENZYMES. SINCE THE NUCLEASES ARE UNABLE TO CLEAVE
THE PROTEIN-BOUND REGIONS OF DNA, WHEN THE CLEAVED DNA FRAGMENTS ARE RUN ON POLYACRYLAMIDE
GEL ELECTROPHORESIS, THERE ARE MISSING BANDS INDICATING, PROTECTED SITES OF PROTEIN-BOUND DNA.
THESE MISSING AREAS REPRESENT THE FOOTPRINT OF THE PROTECTED DNA-PROTEIN COMPLEXES. HENCE DNA
FOOTPRINTING TECHNIQUE HELPS TO IDENTIFY THE SPECIFIC BINDING SITE OF PROTEIN ON A DNA SEQUENCE.
THE IMAGE BELOW ILLUSTRATES THE DNA FOOTPRINTING TECHNIQUE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: DNA FINGERPRINTING USES RFLPS (RESTRICTION FRAGMENT LENGTH POLYMORPHISM) OR REPEAT
SEQUENCE DNA TO IDENTIFY A PERSON'S UNIQUE PATTERN OF DNA. POLYMORPHISMS ARE INHERITED
DIFFERENCES FOUND AMONG INDIVIDUALS. WITH THIS TECHNIQUE, INDIVIDUALS CAN BE DIFFERENTIATED BY
VARIATIONS IN THEIR DNA SEQUENCE, USING RESTRICTION ENDONUCLEASES FOLLOWED BY GEL ELECTROPHORESIS,
TO VISUALIZE RFLPS. DNA FINGERPRINTING IS USED FOR FORENSIC ANALYSIS OF CRIME SCENES, AND FOR
PATERNITY TESTING.
855
OPTION C: ELISA USES ANTIBODIES LINKED TO CERTAIN ENZYMES TO DETECT CERTAIN ANTIGENS PRESENT IN
THE SAMPLE.
OPTION D: NORTHERN BLOTTING TECHNIQUE CAN BE USED TO DETECT RNA. HERE, THE MIXTURE
OF MRNA MOLECULES IS SEPARATED BY ELECTROPHORESIS AND THEN TRANSFERRED TO A NITROCELLULOSE
MEMBRANE AND HYBRIDIZED WITH RADIOLABELED PROBES.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WAS DIAGNOSED WITH EWING SARCOMA WITH EWSR1 GENE MUTATION. THE TECHNIQUE
SHOWN IN THE IMAGE WAS PERFORMED TO CONFIRM THE DIAGNOSIS. IDENTIFY THE TECHNIQUE SHOWN IN
THE IMAGE.
questions.explanation:
THE TECHNIQUE SHOWN IN THE IMAGE IS FISH DEMONSTRATING A POSITIVE EWSR1 GENE REARRANGEMENT,
CHARACTERISTIC OF EWING SARCOMA. THE FUSED REGION DENOTED BY YELLOW CORRESPONDS TO A
NORMAL INTACT GENE, WHILE A SPLIT SIGNAL PATTERN SHOWING SEPARATE RED AND GREEN SIGNALS IS
INDICATIVE OF EWSR1 GENE REARRANGEMENT.
FLUORESCENT IN SITU HYBRIDISATION (FISH) IS A SIMPLE TECHNIQUE FOR THE DETECTION OF SPECIFIC GENETIC
INFORMATION ON MORPHOLOGICALLY INTACT TISSUE USING FLUORESCENT PROBES. FISH CAN BE PERFORMED ON
PRENATAL SAMPLES, PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS, TOUCH PREPARATIONS FROM CANCER BIOPSIES, AND EVEN FIXED
ARCHIVAL TISSUE SECTIONS. IT IS USED TO DETECT
- NUMERIC ABNORMALITIES OF CHROMOSOMES (ANEUPLOIDY)
- SUBTLE MICRODELETIONS AND REARRANGEMENTS.
- COMPLEX TRANSLOCATIONS THAT ARE NOT DEMONSTRABLE BY ROUTINE KARYOTYPING
- GENE AMPLIFICATION (E.G., HER2 IN BREAST CANCER OR NMYC AMPLIFICATION IN NEUROBLASTOMAS)
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: KARYOTYPING IS THE PROCESS BY WHICH CHROMOSOMES ARE ISOLATED, STAINED, AND EXAMINED
TO FIND CHROMOSOMAL ANOMALIES. IT IS USED IN PRENATAL DIAGNOSIS, INVESTIGATION OF REPEAT PREGNANCY
LOSS, INVESTIGATION OF CHILDREN AND ADULTS SUSPECTED OF HAVING A CHROMOSOMAL DISORDER, AND
SUBTYPING OF LYMPHOMAS AND LEUKEMIAS FOR THE PURPOSE OF EXACT DIAGNOSIS, GIVING A PROGNOSIS, AND
TREATMENT.
OPTION C: IHC (IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY) IS A STAINING METHOD FOR HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SPECIMENS. IT
HELPS IN THE DIAGNOSIS AND CLASSIFICATION OF TUMORS BASED ON THEIR DISTINCT PROTEIN EXPRESSION
PATTERNS. EG: THE EXPRESSION OF ESTROGEN RECEPTOR (ER), PROGESTERONE RECEPTOR (PR), AND
HER2/NEU IN BREAST CANCER CELLS IS MAINLY ASSESSED BY IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY.
OPTION D: SANGER'S TECHNIQUE: THIS WAS THE FIRST TECHNIQUE USED TO DETERMINE THE SEQUENCE OF
PROTEINS. THE FIRST PROTEIN TO BE SEQUENCED BY THIS METHOD WAS INSULIN. SANGER’S REAGENT IS 1-
FLOURO 2,4 DINITRO BENZENE. ONLY DIPEPTIDES AND TRIPEPTIDES CAN BE SEQUENCED BY THIS METHOD.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
IN A PATIENT WITH MAPLE SYRUP URINE DISEASE, ALL OF THE FOLLOWING AMINO ACIDS SHOULD BE
RESTRICTED IN DIET EXCEPT?
questions.explanation:
IN MAPLE SYRUP URINE DISEASE (MSUD), ONLY BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS ARE RESTRICTED, HENCE,
METHIONINE DOES NOT NEED ANY RESTRICTION IN DIET.
BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS ARE:
856
- LEUCINE (L)
- ISOLEUCINE (I)
- VALINE (V)
MSUD IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE DISORDER IN WHICH THERE IS A PARTIAL OR COMPLETE DEFICIENCY
OF BRANCHED-CHAIN KETOACID DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX (BCKD). THIS IMPAIRS THE METABOLISM OF
BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS. THESE AMINO ACIDS, PARTICULARLY LEUCINE AND THEIR METABOLITE
ACCUMULATE IN THE BLOOD, CAUSING TOXIC EFFECTS ON THE BRAIN. FEATURES INCLUDE FEEDING PROBLEMS,
VOMITING, KETOSIS, AND A CHARACTERISTIC BURNT SUGAR ODOR /MAPLE SYRUP-LIKE ODOR FOUND
IN URINE, SWEAT, AND CERUMEN.
LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS WILL SHOW INCREASED LEVELS OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS IN THE PLASMA
AND URINE. LEUCINE LEVELS ARE USUALLY HIGHER THAN ISOLEUCINE, AND VALINE.
TREATMENT INVOLVES RESTRICTED INTAKE OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS USING COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE
FORMULAS AND JUDICIOUS SUPPLEMENTATION OF ISOLEUCINE AND VALINE. VERY HIGH LEVELS OF LEUCINE ARE
REMOVED BY HEMODIALYSIS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS ABOUT THE HUMAN GENOME PROJECT IS FALSE?
questions.explanation:
THE HUMAN GENOME PROJECT DID NOT USE NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING.
THE HUMAN GENOME PROJECT (HGP) WAS AN INTERNATIONAL, COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM, WHICH
INVOLVED AGENCIES SUCH AS UNESCO, HUGO, THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF HEALTH/DEPARTMENT OF
ENERGY (USA), THE MEDICAL RESEARCH COUNCIL (UK), GENETHON (FRANCE), AND THE EUROPEAN UNION.
THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THE HUMAN GENOME PROJECT WAS TO DETERMINE THE SEQUENCE OF ALL NUCLEOTIDE
BASE PAIRS, THAT MAKE UP HUMAN DNA AND TO CREATE A SINGLE LINEAR MAP OF ALL GENES FROM THE
HUMAN GENOME. THE PROJECT WAS ACTIVE FROM 1990 TO 2003, TAKING AROUND 13 YEARS TO COMPLETE. A
TOTAL OF 20500 GENES WERE IDENTIFIED AND MAPPED. SCIENTISTS USED VARIOUS METHODS
OF FIRST-GENERATION SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES INCLUDING SANGER'S TECHNIQUE, SGS TECHNIQUE, ETC. THE
HGP HAS PRODUCED A CURATED AND ACCURATE REFERENCE SEQUENCE FOR THE MAJORITY OF HUMAN
857
CHROMOSOMES. THE REFERENCE SEQUENCE HAS PROVIDED THE FOUNDATION FOR THE USE OF
SECOND-GENERATION SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS ARRAY TECHNIQUES.
NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING (NGS) IS A NEW TECHNOLOGY USED FOR SEQUENCING DNA AND RNA AND
MUTATION DETECTION. NGS CAN SEQUENCE THE GENOME FASTER AND IN A SHORTER PERIOD OF TIME THAN
FIRST-GENERATION SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES. NGS ALLOWS FOR THE DETECTION OF A SPECTRUM OF
MUTATIONS, INCLUDING SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE SUBSTITUTIONS, SMALL INSERTIONS AND DELETIONS, LARGE GENOMIC
DUPLICATIONS AND DELETIONS, AND RARE VARIATIONS. NEXT-GENERATION DNA SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES
INCLUDE
- ILLUMINA SEQUENCING
- ROCHE 454 SEQUENCING
- ION TORRENT: PROTON/PGM SEQUENCING
- SOLID SEQUENCING.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: BANDING TECHNIQUE USED FOR DICENTRIC CHROMOSOMES IS:
questions.explanation:
THE BANDING TECHNIQUE USED FOR DICENTRIC CHROMOSOMES IS C BANDING.
HETEROCHROMATIN INCLUDES NON-CODING REGIONS OF DNA, SUCH AS CENTROMERIC REGIONS. THE STAINING
OF THESE CONSTITUTIVE HETEROCHROMATINS, IS DONE BY C-BANDING USING SILVER SALT STAINING. A DICENTRIC
CHROMOSOME HAVING TWO CENTROMERES CAN HENCE BE IDENTIFIED BY C BANDING.
VARIOUS TECHNIQUES ARE USED IN KARYOTYPING TO STUDY CHROMOSOMES. STAINING WITH VARIOUS
COMPOUNDS PRODUCES VARIOUS RESULTS AND HELPS US TO UNDERSTAND THE CHROMOSOMES BETTER.
COMMON TECHNIQUES USED ARE:
- Q BANDING - FLUORESCENCE STAINING WITH QUINACRINE MUSTARD.
- G BANDING - GIEMSA STAINING AFTER PARTIAL DENATURATION OF CHROMATIN. IT IS THE MOST COMMON
TECHNIQUE USED IN CYTOGENETICS TO PRODUCE A VISIBLE KARYOTYPE BY STAINING CONDENSED
CHROMOSOMES.
- R BANDING - REVERSE GIEMSA STAINING. IN THIS, THE LIGHT AND DARK AREAS ARE REVERSED.
- C BANDING - STAINING OF HETEROCHROMATIN WITH SILVER SALTS.
- T BANDING - STAINING THE TELOMERES OF CHROMOSOMES.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: AFFINITY MATURATION OF ANTIBODIES IS BECAUSE OF?
questions.explanation:
AFFINITY MATURATION OF ANTIBODIES IS BECAUSE OF SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION.
AFFINITY MATURATION IS THE PROCESS BY WHICH ANTIBODIES GAIN
INCREASED AFFINITY, AVIDITY, AND ANTI-PATHOGEN ACTIVITY. IT IS A RESULT OF SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION OF
IMMUNOGLOBULIN GENES IN B CELLS, COUPLED WITH SELECTION FOR ANTIGEN BINDING.
SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION IS A CELLULAR RESPONSE BY WHICH THE IMMUNE SYSTEM ADAPTS TO THE NEW
FOREIGN ELEMENTS THAT CONFRONT IT. THEY DO SO BY ADDING NUCLEOTIDES IN V GENE REGIONS OF HEAVY AND
858
LIGHT CHAINS, RESULTING IN A BETTER FIT OF ANTIGEN WITH THE ANTIBODIES. THIS HENCE INCREASES THE
AFFINITY OF ANTIBODIES TO ANTIGENS. DUE TO THIS, THE SUBSET OF PLASMA CELLS WITH THESE IMPROVED
HYPERVARIABLE REGIONS ARE MORE STRONGLY
SELECTED BY THE ANTIGEN AND THEREFORE CONSTITUTE A LARGER PART OF THE POPULATION OF
ANTIBODY-PRODUCING CELLS. THIS PROCESS IS CALLED AFFINITY MATURATION.
THIS PROCESS OCCURS IN THE GERMINAL CENTERS AND PROCEEDS FOR WEEKS AFTER ACUTE INFECTION OR
VACCINATION, OR FOR MANY CYCLES DURING CHRONIC INFECTION. THE RESULTING ANTIBODIES CAN BE HIGHLY
MUTATED FROM THEIR GERMLINE-ENCODED COUNTERPARTS, WITH AN INCREASE IN SEVERAL ORDERS OF
MAGNITUDE IN AFFINITY FOR ANTIGEN COMPARED TO THE CORRESPONDING NAïVE B CELL RECEPTORS (BCRS).

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: BEST METHOD FOR DETECTION OF MUTATIONS WITH LOW ALLELE FREQUENCY IS
questions.explanation:
BEST METHOD FOR DETECTION OF MUTATION WITH LOW ALLELE FREQUENCY IS DROPLET DIGITAL PCR (DDPCR)
IT IS AN ADVANCED AND MORE PRECISE TYPE OF QUANTITATIVE PCR WHICH GIVES MORE CONSISTENT AND
REPRODUCIBLE RESULTS. IT CAN ACCURATELY QUANTIFY THE TARGET NUCLEIC ACID SEQUENCE WITHIN A SAMPLE. IT
IS USEFUL FOR DETERMINING SOMATIC MUTATION WITH LOW ALLELE FREQUENCY. MUTANT ALLELES OF FREQUENCY
AS LOW AS 0.25% CAN ALSO BE DETECTED USING THIS TECHNIQUE.
POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION (PCR) IS A RAPID AUTOMATED METHOD FOR THE AMPLIFICATION OF SPECIFIC
DNA SEQUENCES (OR GENES). REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE PCR- THE ENZYME REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE (RT) IS
USED TO SYNTHESIZE A COMPLIMENTARY COPY OF DNA (CDNA) FROM RNA AND THIS CDNA IS THEN USED
AS A TEMPLATE FOR PCR.
OTHER SPECIAL PCR TYPES:
NESTED PCR- IT INVOLVES THE SEQUENTIAL USE OF TWO PRIMER SETS. THE FIRST PRIMER SET IS USED FOR
AMPLIFICATION AND THE TARGET SEQUENCE FOR THE SECOND PRIMER IS PRESENT ONLY ON THE AMPLICON WITH
THE TARGET SEQUENCE. NESTED PCR IS INTENDED TO REDUCE NON-SPECIFIC BINDING DUE TO THE
AMPLIFICATION OF UNEXPECTED PRIMER BINDING SITES.
859
MULTIPLEX PCR- MULTIPLE PRIMERS ARE USED TO AMPLIFY SEVERAL DNA SEQUENCES SIMULTANEOUSLY. AS
THIS PROCESS TARGETS MULTIPLE GENES AT ONCE, A SINGLE TEST RUN GIVES ADDITIONAL INFORMATION THAT
WOULD OTHERWISE REQUIRE SEVERAL TIMES THE REAGENTS AND TECHNICIAN TIME TO PERFORM.
THE SANGER SEQUENCING TECHNIQUE IS USED FOR DNA SEQUENCING. IT IS BASED ON CONTROLLED
TERMINATION OF SYNTHESIS OF DNA BY USING CHAIN TERMINATING AGENTS LIKE DIDEOXYNUCLEOTIDES.
FLUORESCENT IN SITU HYBRIDISATION (FISH) IS A SIMPLE TECHNIQUE FOR THE DETECTION OF SPECIFIC GENETIC
INFORMATION ON MORPHOLOGICALLY INTACT TISSUE USING FLUORESCENT PROBES. FISH CAN BE PERFORMED ON
PRENATAL SAMPLES, PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS, TOUCH PREPARATIONS FROM CANCER BIOPSIES, AND EVEN FIXED
ARCHIVAL TISSUE SECTIONS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: IN SANGER SEQUENCING, DDNTP IS USED BECAUSE:
options: IT IS USED TO INCREASE DNA POLYMERASE ACTIVITY
THEY EXHIBIT HIGHER AFFINITY FOR DNA POLYMERASES
IT DOESN'T ALLOW FURTHER ELONGATION OF DNA
questions.answer: IT DOESN'T ALLOW FURTHER ELONGATION OF DNA
questions.explanation:
IN SANGER SEQUENCING, DIDEOXYNUCLEOTIDES TRIPHOSPHATES (DDNTP) ARE USED BECAUSE IT DOESN'T
ALLOW FURTHER ELONGATION OF DNA.
THE SANGER METHOD IS USED FOR DNA SEQUENCING. THIS METHOD USES THE MECHANISM OF SYNTHESIS OF
DNA BY DNA POLYMERASES. IN THE PROCESS OF SYNTHESIS OF DNA, THE 3'-HYDROXYL GROUP OF PRIMER
REACTS WITH AN INCOMING DNTP TO FORM A NEW PHOSPHODIESTER BOND. THIS REACTION IS CATALYZED BY
DNA POLYMERASE.
IN THE SANGER SEQUENCING METHOD, DDNTP IS USED BECAUSE IT HALTS THE DNA SYNTHESIS. DDNTPS CAN
BIND TO THE TEMPLATE STRAND BUT LACK THE 3'-HYDROXYL GROUP WHICH IS REQUIRED TO ADD THE NEXT
NUCLEOTIDE. THE PRODUCTS OF THIS REACTION ARE A MIXTURE OF DNA STRANDS OF VARYING LENGTHS. THIS
MIXTURE IS THEN SEPARATED USING POLYACRYLAMIDE GEL ELECTROPHORESIS AND AUTORADIOGRAPHY. THIS
PRODUCES A PATTERN OF BANDS FROM WHICH THE DNA SEQUENCE CAN BE READ.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE STEPS INVOLVED IN SANGER'S METHOD.
SANGER’S TECHNIQUE WAS THE FIRST TECHNIQUE USED TO DETERMINE THE SEQUENCE OF PROTEINS. THE FIRST
PROTEIN TO BE SEQUENCED BY THIS METHOD WAS INSULIN. SANGER’S REAGENT IS 1- FLUORO 2,4 DINITRO
BENZENE.
860

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: MISINCORPORATION OF URACIL INTO DNA IS SEEN IN DEFICIENCY OF:
questions.explanation:
MISINCORPORATION OF URACIL INTO DNA IS SEEN IN THE DEFICIENCY OF FOLATE.
FOLATE DEFICIENCY LEADS TO DECREASED THYMIDYLATE SYNTHESIS FROM DEOXYURIDYLATE DUE TO DEFICIENT
METHYLATION OF DEOXYURIDINE MONOPHOSPHATE (DUMP) TO THYMIDINE MONOPHOSPHATE (TMP). THE
METHYLATION OF DUMP TO TMP IS CATALYZED BY THYMIDYLATE SYNTHASE AND
REQUIRES TETRAHYDROFOLATE (THFA) AS A METHYL GROUP DONOR. THIS DECREASED TMP SYNTHESIS
CAN RESULT IN AN IMBALANCE OF DEOXYRIBONUCLEOTIDES AND HENCE LEADING TO EXCESSIVE URACIL
MISINCORPORATION INTO DNA DURING REPLICATION AND REPAIR.
FOLIC ACID (VITAMIN B9) IS A WATER-SOLUBLE VITAMIN, AND ITS ACTIVE FORM IS TETRAHYDROFOLATE (THFA).
IT ACTS AS A CARRIER OF ONE-CARBON GROUPS. TETRAHYDROFOLATE RECEIVES ONE-CARBON
FRAGMENTS FROM DONORS SUCH AS SERINE, GLYCINE, AND HISTIDINE AND TRANSFERS THEM TO INTERMEDIATES
IN THE SYNTHESIS OF AMINO ACIDS, PURINES, AND PYRIMIDINES.
FOLATE DEFICIENCY RESULTS IN:
- MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA
- HOMOCYSTENEMIA
- NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS (SPINA BIFIDA, ANENCEPHALY) IN THE FETUS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: DEAMINATION OF METHYLATED CYTOSINE FORMS WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING?
questions.explanation:
DEAMINATION OF METHYLATED CYTOSINE FORMS THYMINE.
DEAMINATION IS THE REMOVAL OF AN AMINO GROUP(NH2) FROM A CHEMICAL COMPOUND. ENZYMES THAT
CATALYZE THIS REACTION ARE CALLED DEAMINASES. DEAMINATION OF 5-METHYLCYTOSINE FORMS THYMINE.
OTHER SIGNIFICANT DEAMINATIONS ARE GIVEN BELOW:
861
- DEAMINATION OF ADENOSINE FORMS INOSINE. THIS IS A METABOLIC STEP INVOLVED IN URIC ACID FORMATION
BY PURINE CATABOLISM. IT IS MEDIATED BY THE ENZYME ADENOSINE DEAMINASE (ADA). ADA DEFICIENCY
LEADS TO SPARSE OR DEFECTIVE T CELLS AND B CELLS AND PATIENTS SUFFER FROM SEVERE COMBINED
IMMUNODEFICIENCY (SCID).
- DEAMINATION OF CYTOSINE LEADS TO URACIL FORMATION - THE PRODUCTION OF APOLIPOPROTEIN B-48
(APOB-48) IN THE INTESTINE IS THE RESULT OF RNA EDITING IN THE INTESTINE. THIS INVOLVES
POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL DEAMINATION OF CYTOSINE TO URACIL BY ENZYME CYTIDINE DEAMINASE.
THIS CONVERTS SENSE CODON (CAA) IN THE MRNA TO NONSENSE CODON (UAA)AT A SINGLE SPECIFIC
SITE. THIS EDITED MRNA TRANSLATES TO APOB-48.
- DEAMINATION OF GUANINE FORMS XANTHINE. THIS IS A METABOLIC STEP INVOLVED IN URIC ACID FORMATION
BY PURINE CATABOLISM.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING TYPES OF INHIBITION IS DEPICTED IN THE GIVEN LINEWEAVER-BURK PLOT?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN GRAPH SHOWS COMPETITIVE INHIBITION, IN WHICH THE VALUE OF VMAX REMAINS CONSTANT AND
THE KM VALUE INCREASES.
- KM IS THE SUBSTRATE CONCENTRATION AT WHICH VELOCITY IS HALF MAXIMUM.
- VMAX IS THE MAXIMUM VELOCITY OF A REACTION.
COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS WHEN THE INHIBITOR BINDS REVERSIBLY TO THE SUBSTRATE-BINDING SITE AND
COMPETES WITH THE SUBSTRATE FOR THE ACTIVE ENZYME-BINDING SITE. THIS EFFECT OF COMPETITIVE
INHIBITION CAN BE OVERCOME BY INCREASING THE SUBSTRATE CONCENTRATION BY WHICH MAXIMUM VELOCITY
CAN STILL BE ACHIEVED. THEREFORE, VMAX IS UNALTERED IN THIS TYPE OF INHIBITION. HOWEVER, THE
CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE HALF OF THE MAXIMUM VELOCITY IS INCREASED.
THEREFORE, KM IS INCREASED IN THIS CONDITION.
THE GRAPH SHOWS THE CHANGES IN VMAX AND KM IN COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.

OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS BY BINDING INHIBITORS TO ENZYMES IN LOCATIONS
REMOTE FROM THE ACTIVE SITE. INCREASING THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE DOES NOT OVERCOME
NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION. THUS, NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS DECREASE THE VMAX OF THE REACTION.
THEY DO NOT INTERFERE WITH THE BINDING OF THE SUBSTRATE TO THE ENZYME. THUS, THE ENZYME SHOWS
THE SAME KM IN THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS.
THE GRAPH SHOWS THE CHANGES IN VMAX AND KM IN NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.
OPTION C: IN UNCOMPETITIVE INHIBITION, INHIBITORS BIND WITH THE ENZYME-SUBSTRATE INTERMEDIATE
COMPLEX, AND INHIBIT IT. THIS LEADS TO DECREASE IN BOTH VMAX AND KM. AN EXAMPLE IS THE INHIBITION
OF PLACENTAL ALKALINE PHOSPHATE (ALP) BY PHENYLALANINE.
OPTION D: SUICIDAL INHIBITION IS A SPECIAL TYPE OF IRREVERSIBLE INHIBITION. THE INHIBITOR HERE MAKES
USE OF THE ENZYME'S OWN REACTION MECHANISM TO INACTIVATE IT AND IS HENCE KNOWN AS
MECHANISM-BASED INACTIVATION. AN EXAMPLE IS ALLOPURINOL, WHICH IS OXIDIZED BY XANTHINE OXIDASE
863
TO ALLOXANTHINE. ALLOXANTHINE IN TURN IS A MORE POTENT INHIBITOR OF XANTHINE OXIDASE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE IS ACTIVATED BY:
questions.explanation:
GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE IS ACTIVATED BY CALCIUM IN THE MUSCLE.
GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE IS THE RATE-LIMITING ENZYME OF GLYCOGENOLYSIS AND IS DECREASED IN THE FED
STATE.
IN THE MUSCLE, THE INCREASED CYTOSOLIC CALCIUM ION CONCENTRATION INITIATES BOTH CONTRACTION AND
GLYCOGENOLYSIS. MUSCLE PHOSPHORYLASE KINASE HAS FOUR DIFFERENT SUBUNITS, α, β, γ, AND δ. THE α AND
β SUBUNITS ARE PHOSPHORYLATED BY CAMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASE. THE δ SUBUNIT IS IDENTICAL TO
THE CALCIUM-BINDING PROTEIN CALMODULIN AND BINDS FOUR CALCIUM IONS. CALCIUM COORDINATES THE
ACTIVATION OF GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE WITH THE CONTRACTION OF THE MUSCLE.
GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE CATALYZES THE CLEAVAGE OF α1 → 4 LINKAGES OF GLYCOGEN TO SINGLE UNITS OF
GLUCOSE 1-PHOSPHATE. IT USES PYRIDOXAL PHOSPHATE AS THE COENZYME. DIFFERENT ISOENZYMES OF
GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE ARE SEEN IN THE LIVER, MUSCLES, AND BRAIN.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: DURING GLYCOGENOLYSIS, GLUCOSE 6-PHOSPHATE ALLOSTERICALLY INHIBITS GLYCOGEN
PHOSPHORYLASE.
OPTION C: INSULIN ENTIRELY SUPPRESSES GLYCOGENOLYSIS IN THE SKELETAL MUSCLE AND LIVER.
OPTION D: IN GLYCOGENOLYSIS PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE IS INACTIVATED BY INHIBITOR PROTEINS IN RESPONSE TO
CAMP, TO MAINTAIN THE GLYCOGEN PHOSPHORYLASE IN AN ACTIVE STATE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: MUTATION OF THE GENE OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS OCCURS WITH:
questions.explanation:
THE MUTANT GENE OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS (CF GENE) PRODUCES A MUTANT CFTR PROTEIN WITH THE DELETION OF
A PHENYLALANINE RESIDUE AT 508 (F508DEL), CHARACTERISED BY IMPAIRED CHLORIDE SECRETION.
CYSTIC FIBROSIS IS A CONDITION WITH AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE MODE OF INHERITANCE. IT RESULTS DUE TO A
DEFECTIVE MUTATION IN THE GENE ENCODING FOR CYSTIC FIBROSIS TRANSMEMBRANE CONDUCTANCE REGULATOR
(CF GENE). IT PLAYS AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN MUCOCILIARY TRANSPORT ALONG THE RESPIRATORY MUCOSA. IT ALSO
HELPS TO REGULATE THE AMOUNT OF EXOCRINE GLAND SECRETION.
THE DEFECT IN THE ION CHANNEL RESULTS IN THE PRODUCTION OF HYPER-VISCOUS, ADHERENT SECRETIONS
WHICH CAN OBSTRUCT THE AIRWAYS. ORGANISMS SUCH AS PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS
AUREUS CAN GROW IN THE SPUTUM. THE EXOCRINE PANCREAS CAN UNDERGO FIBROTIC SCARRING, CYST
FORMATION, AND ACINAR TISSUE LOSS. THE VISCID SECRETIONS CAN LEAD TO PANCREATIC DUCT OBSTRUCTION.
THE FLOW OF DIGESTIVE ENZYMES TO THE DUODENUM IS HENCE IMPAIRED.
SYMPTOMS INCLUDE SINUSITIS, STEATORRHEA, AND ABDOMINAL PAIN. DISTAL INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION IS A
COMPLICATION DUE TO DIFFICULTY IN EXCRETING INTESTINAL CONTENTS. IN NEONATES, IT CAN PRESENT AS
MECONIUM ILEUS.
DETECTION OF HIGH LEVELS OF TRYPSINOGEN IS USED IN NEWBORN SCREENING. CHLORIDE LEVEL >60MEQ/L
IN THE SWEAT OF AFFECTED PATIENTS IS DIAGNOSTIC. HYPONATREMIC HYPOCHLOREMIC ALKALOSIS IS SEEN.
864
POSTURAL DRAINAGE, SHORT-TERM ANTIBIOTICS, AND INHALED BRONCHODILATORS CAN BE USED FOR MEDICAL
MANAGEMENT. THE DEFINITIVE TREATMENT IS LUNG TRANSPLANTATION.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS THE FEATURES OF THE DISEASE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A BABY IS BROUGHT TO THE OPD WITH COMPLAINTS OF LETHARGY AND POOR FEEDING. ON EXAMINATION,
IT IS NOTED THAT THE URINE HAD A SMELL OF BURNT SUGAR. A DEFECT IN WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING
ENZYMES CAUSES THIS DISEASE?
questions.explanation:
THE DIAGNOSIS, IN THIS CASE, IS THAT OF MAPLE SYRUP URINE DISEASE (MSUD). THIS DISEASE OCCURS DUE
TO A DEFECT OF THE ENZYME BRANCHED-CHAIN KETO ACID DEHYDROGENASE.
MSUD IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE DISORDER THAT OCCURS DUE TO A DEFICIENCY OF BRANCHED-CHAIN
KETOACID DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX. THIS IMPAIRS THE METABOLISM OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS
VALINE, LEUCINE, ISOLEUCINE, AND ALLOISOLEUCINE. THESE AMINO ACIDS, PARTICULARLY LEUCINE AND ITS
METABOLITE ACCUMULATE IN THE BLOOD, CAUSING TOXIC EFFECTS ON THE BRAIN.
THE AFFECTED CHILD DEVELOPS POOR FEEDING AND VOMITING A FEW DAYS AFTER BIRTH. THERE IS A PERIOD OF
HYPERTONICITY WITH A PERIOD OF FLACCIDITY IN BETWEEN. THESE APPEAR AS REPETITIVE BOXING AND
BICYCLING MOVEMENTS. THE BABIES MAY ALSO HAVE HYPOGLYCEMIA, BUT THIS IS NOT CORRECTED BY THE
ADMINISTRATION OF GLUCOSE. THE URINE, SWEAT, AND CERUMEN OF THE BABY HAVE A SWEETISH MAPLE
SYRUP-LIKE ODOR.
LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS WILL SHOW INCREASED LEVELS OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS IN THE PLASMA
AND URINE. LEUCINE LEVELS ARE USUALLY HIGHER THAN ISOLEUCINE, VALINE, AND ALLOISOLEUCINE. SINCE THE
PATIENT EXCRETES KETONE BODIES IN THE URINE, THE URINE WILL BE POSITIVE FOR THE
DINITROPHENYLHYDRAZINE TEST.
TREATMENT INVOLVES CONTROLLED INTAKE OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACIDS USING COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE
FORMULAS AND JUDICIOUS SUPPLEMENTATION OF ISOLEUCINE AND VALINE. VERY HIGH LEVELS OF LEUCINE ARE
REMOVED BY HEMODIALYSIS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: ALL ARE TRUE ABOUT THE HEXOSE MONOPHOSPHATE SHUNT, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
865
THE HEXOSE MONOPHOSPHATE (HMP) SHUNT PRODUCES RIBOSE AND DOES NOT UTILIZE IT.
THE PENTOSE PHOSPHATE PATHWAY, ALSO KNOWN AS THE HMP SHUNT PATHWAY, IS AN ALTERNATIVE ROUTE
FOR THE METABOLISM OF GLUCOSE. IT CONTRIBUTES IN TWO MAJOR WAYS:
- FORMATION OF NADPH FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF FATTY ACIDS AND STEROIDS AND MAINTENANCE OF REDUCED
GLUTATHIONE FOR ANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY.
- FORMATION OF RIBOSE FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF NUCLEIC ACID AND NUCLEOTIDES
THE ENZYMES FOR THIS PATHWAY ARE FOUND IN THE CYTOSOL. THERE ARE TWO PHASES:
- IRREVERSIBLE OXIDATIVE PHASE: GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE IS DEHYDROGENATED AND DECARBOXYLATED TO
FORM RIBULOSE-5-PHOSPHATE WHICH IN TURN GETS CONVERTED TO RIBOSE-5-PHOSPHATE.
- REVERSIBLE NON-OXIDATIVE PHASE: RIBULOSE-5-PHOSPHATE IS CONVERTED BACK TO GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING ENZYMES USE SELENOCYSTEINE?
questions.explanation:
THE ENZYMES THAT USE SELENOCYSTEINE ARE GLUTATHIONE PEROXIDASE, DEIODINASE, AND THIOREDOXIN
REDUCTASE.
SELENOCYSTEINE IS THE 21ST AMINO ACID CODED BY THE UGA CODON, WHICH IS NORMALLY A STOP CODON. IT
IS FORMED BY CO-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATION. THE PROTEIN SYNTHETIC APPARATUS CAN IDENTIFY A
SELENOCYSTEINE-ENCODING UGA BY THE PRESENCE OF THE SELENOCYSTEINE INSERTION SEQUENCE (SECIS) IN
THE UNTRANSLATED REGION OF MRNA.
ENZYMES SUCH AS THIOREDOXIN REDUCTASE, GLUTATHIONE PEROXIDASE, AND DEIODINASE USE
SELENOCYSTEINE TO CATALYZE REDOX REACTIONS. DEFECTS IN HUMAN SELENOPROTEINS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH
TUMORIGENESIS AND ATHEROSCLEROSIS. IT CAN CAUSE CARDIOMYOPATHY DUE TO SELENIUM DEFICIENCY, WHICH
IS KNOWN AS KESHAN DISEASE.
GLUTATHIONE SYNTHASE IS THE SECOND ENZYME IN THE SYNTHESIS OF GLUTATHIONE. GLUTATHIONE PLAYS AN
IMPORTANT ROLE IN OXIDATIVE STRESS, REDOX SIGNALLING, AND REGULATES CELL PROLIFERATION AND APOPTOSIS.
866

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH REDUCED LEVELS OF HIGH-DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN, AND ABCA1 MUTATION. ON
EXAMINATION, TONSILS APPEARED AS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE. WHAT IS THE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS CASE WITH REDUCED LEVELS OF HIGH-DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN (HDL), ABCA1 MUTATION,
AND ORANGE TONSILS ON EXAMINATION IS TANGIER'S DISEASE. IT IS CAUSED BY A DEFECT IN ABCA1
RECEPTORS.
ABCA1 PLAYS A ROLE IN THE EFFLUX OF CHOLESTEROL FROM PERIPHERAL CELLS OF HDL. LCAT (LECITHIN
CHOLESTEROL ACYLTRANSFERASE) CONVERTS CHOLESTEROL TO CHOLESTEROL ESTERS, WHICH ACCUMULATE IN THE
CORE OF HDL. THUS, DEFECTIVE ABCA1 WILL LEAD TO LOW LEVELS OF HDL IN THE BLOOD.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: ABETALIPOPROTEINEMIA IS A HYPOLIPOPROTEINEMIA CAUSED BY A DEFECT IN THE MTP GENE.
HERE, LOADING APOLIPOPROTEIN B WITH LIPIDS IS DEFECTIVE. HENCE, FEW VERY LOW DENSITY-LIPOPROTEINS
(VLDLS) OR CHYLOMICRONS ARE FORMED, LEADING TO THE ACCUMULATION OF TRIACYLGLYCEROLS IN THE LIVER
AND INTESTINE.
OPTION C: HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA IS A DISORDER THAT CAUSES THE BODY TO METABOLIZE LIPIDS
INCORRECTLY. THIS RESULTS IN HYPERLIPIDEMIA AND CAN LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF MULTIPLE SMALL
XANTHOMAS IN THE SKIN.
OPTION D: ACID LIPASE DEFICIENCY CAN LEAD TO WOLMAN'S DISEASE WHICH IS A LYSOSOMAL STORAGE
DISEASE. THE PATHOGNOMIC FEATURE OF THIS CONDITION IS ADRENAL CALCIFICATION. SO PATIENTS GENERALLY
PRESENT WITH ADRENAL INSUFFICIENCY AND ARE NEONATES.
